remote_backup_site.name: Remote Backup Site
remote_backup_site.definition: A site where all the data from the primary site are replicated.

secondary_site.name: Secondary Site
secondary_site.definition: Another term for the remote backup site.

log_records.name: Log Records
log_records.definition: Records sent from the primary site to the remote backup site to maintain synchronization.

infrastructure_as_service.name: Infrastructure-as-Service Model
infrastructure_as_service.definition: A cloud service model where the client enterprise runs its own software, including database systems, on virtual machines provided by the cloud service provider.

platform_as_a_service.name: Platform-as-a-Service Model
platform_as_a_service.definition: A cloud service model where the service provider not only provides computing infrastructure but also deploys and manages platforms such as data storage, databases, and application servers.

cloud_based_data_storage_platform.name: Cloud-Based Data Storage Platform
cloud_based_data_storage_platform.definition: A service that applications can use to store and retrieve data, managed by the service provider.

persistent_data_storage.name: Persistent Data Storage
persistent_data_storage.definition: Non-volatile storage where data are stored permanently.

magnetic_disk.name: Magnetic Disk
magnetic_disk.definition: A type of non-volatile storage device.

ssd.name: SSD
ssd.definition: A type of non-volatile storage device.

block_structured_device.name: Block Structured Device
block_structured_device.definition: A storage device that reads or writes data in units of a block.

os_file.name: OS File
os_file.definition: An intermediate layer used by most databases for storing records.

block.name: Block
block.definition: The unit of data read or written by a block structured device.

data_dictionary.name: Data Dictionary
data_dictionary.definition: Information about the relational schemas and storage organization in a database.

fixed_length_records.name: Fixed-Length Records
fixed_length_records.definition: A method of organizing files where each record has a fixed size.

file_header.name: File Header
file_header.definition: A section at the beginning of a file that contains metadata about the file.

deleted_record.name: Deleted Record
deleted_record.definition: A record in a file that has been marked as deleted but still occupies space.

linked_list.name: Linked List
linked_list.definition: A linear collection of data elements, called nodes, each pointing to the next node by means of a pointer.

user_u1.name: User U1
user_u1.definition: A user who wants to share data with another user.

user_u2.name: User U2
user_u2.definition: A user who receives encrypted data from another user.

e2_public_key.name: E2 Public Key
e2_public_key.definition: The public key of User U2 used for encrypting data.

private_key_pair_p1_p2.name: (P1, P2) Private Key Pair
private_key_pair_p1_p2.definition: The private key consisting of two large prime numbers P1 and P2.

product_p1_p2.name: P1 * P2 Product
product_p1_p2.definition: The product of two large prime numbers P1 and P2, which is part of the public key.

b_plus_tree_node.name: B+ Tree Node
b_plus_tree_node.definition: A structure used in B+ trees.

cache_line.name: Cache Line
cache_line.definition: A unit of data that fits into a cache.

large_b_plus_tree_node.name: Large B+ Tree Node
large_b_plus_tree_node.definition: A B+ tree node with larger size to optimize disk-based access.

smaller_node.name: Smaller Node
smaller_node.definition: A node within a large B+ tree node that matches the size of a cache line.

replica.name: Replica
replica.definition: A component storing a copy of data items.

hash_function_h1.name: Hash Function h1
hash_function_h1.definition: A function that hashes each data item key to get a hash value with n bits.

hash_function_h2.name: Hash Function h2
hash_function_h2.definition: A function that hashes each data item value to get a hash value.

hash_function_h3.name: Hash Function h3
hash_function_h3.definition: A function that takes as input a collection of hash values and returns a hash value computed from the collection.

isa_relationship.name: ISA Relationship
isa_relationship.definition: A relationship where a lower-level entity set is part of a higher-level entity set in a hierarchy.

single_inheritance.name: Single Inheritance
single_inheritance.definition: An entity set can be involved as a lower-level entity set in only one ISA relationship.

multiple_inheritance.name: Multiple Inheritance
multiple_inheritance.definition: An entity set can be involved as a lower-level entity set in more than one ISA relationship.

lattice.name: Lattice
lattice.definition: A structure resulting from an entity set having multiple ISA relationships.

cartesian_product_operation.name: Cartesian Product Operation
cartesian_product_operation.definition: A relational algebra operation that constructs a new relation from every possible combination of tuples from two input relations.

rename_operation.name: Rename Operation
rename_operation.definition: An operation used to avoid naming conflicts when using the result of a relational algebra expression in a Cartesian product.

teaches_relation.name: Teaches Relation
teaches_relation.definition: A relation containing tuples representing teaching assignments.

r_relation.name: Relation r
r_relation.definition: A relation resulting from the Cartesian product of the instructor and teaches relations.

transaction_requirements.name: Transaction Requirements
transaction_requirements.definition: The needs of organizations to query large databases or process a large number of transactions per second.

parallel_database_systems.name: Parallel Database Systems
parallel_database_systems.definition: Database systems designed to handle extremely large databases or a large number of transactions per second.

centralized_database_systems.name: Centralized Database Systems
centralized_database_systems.definition: Database systems where all data and processing are performed on a single node.

client_server_database_systems.name: Client-Server Database Systems
client_server_database_systems.definition: Database systems where data and processing are distributed between a server and multiple clients.

web_scale_applications.name: Web-Scale Applications
web_scale_applications.definition: Applications that require hundreds to thousands of nodes to handle vast numbers of users.

decision_support_queries.name: Decision-Support Queries
decision_support_queries.definition: Queries used for planning activities and pricing based on large volumes of data.

main_memory.name: Main Memory
main_memory.definition: Large and cheap enough to fit all operational data in-memory.

cache_memory.name: Cache Memory
cache_memory.definition: Memory component with faster access compared to main memory.

multilevel_index.name: Multilevel Index
multilevel_index.definition: Indices with two or more levels.

inner_index.name: Inner Index
inner_index.definition: A component of a multilevel index that occupies 1,000,000 blocks with a 100,000,000 tuple relation.

outer_index.name: Outer Index
outer_index.definition: A component of a multilevel index that occupies 10,000 blocks with a 100,000,000 tuple relation.

binary_tree.name: Binary Tree
binary_tree.definition: A tree structure used for in-memory indexing.

distributed_query_processing.name: Distributed Query Processing
distributed_query_processing.definition: A process for executing queries across multiple databases that are often geographically distributed.

multiple_databases.name: Multiple Databases
multiple_databases.definition: Databases that are often geographically distributed.

lock_de_escalation.name: Lock De-escalation
lock_de_escalation.definition: A way of adaptively decreasing the lock granularity if there is higher contention.

data_server.name: Data Server
data_server.definition: A component that sends requests to clients to de-escalate locks.

client.name: Client
client.definition: A component that responds to lock de-escalation requests and acquires finer-granularity locks.

coarse_granularity_lock.name: Coarse-Granularity Lock
coarse_granularity_lock.definition: A type of lock with a broader scope.

fine_granularity_lock.name: Fine-Granularity Lock
fine_granularity_lock.definition: A type of lock with a narrower scope.

cached_data_item.name: Cached Data Item
cached_data_item.definition: A data item stored in a cache.

sha_256.name: SHA-256
sha_256.definition: A cryptographic hash function that generates a 256-bit output.

collision_resistant_hash_function.name: Collision Resistant Hash Function
collision_resistant_hash_function.definition: A hash function where it is infeasible to find two distinct values x and y such that h(x) = h(y).

association_rule.name: Association Rule
association_rule.definition: A rule that describes the likelihood of two items being bought together.

population.name: Population
population.definition: A set of instances used in association rules.

instance.name: Instance
instance.definition: An individual purchase in the context of association rules.

different_course_offerings.name: Different Course Offerings
different_course_offerings.definition: Courses with the same identifier but different titles.

course_entity.name: Course Entity

course_offering_entity.name: Course Offering Entity
course_offering_entity.definition: A component representing a specific offering of a course.

sale_entity.name: Sale Entity
sale_entity.definition: An entity representing the act of a customer buying a product.

customer_entity.name: Customer Entity
customer_entity.definition: A component representing a customer in the design process.

product_entity.name: Product Entity
product_entity.definition: A component representing a product in the design process.

majority_based_protocol.name: Majority-Based Protocol
majority_based_protocol.definition: A protocol that uses a majority of replicas to ensure robustness.

buffer_block.name: Buffer Block
buffer_block.definition: A block of data stored in buffer memory.

buffer_manager.name: Buffer Manager
buffer_manager.definition: A component responsible for managing buffer blocks.

pin_operation.name: Pin Operation
pin_operation.definition: An operation that prevents a buffer block from being evicted.

unpin_operation.name: Unpin Operation
unpin_operation.definition: An operation that allows a buffer block to be evicted.

online_index_creation.name: Online Index Creation
online_index_creation.definition: A method of creating an index on a relation while the relation is being updated.

shared_lock.name: Shared Lock
shared_lock.definition: A type of lock that allows multiple transactions to read the same data simultaneously but prevents other transactions from modifying the data.

replication_across_racks.name: Replication Across Racks
replication_across_racks.definition: Replicating partitions to a node on a different rack to deal with rack failures.

replication_across_data_centers.name: Replication Across Data Centers
replication_across_data_centers.definition: Replicating partitions to one or more geographically separated data centers to deal with the failure of an entire data center.

geographic_separation.name: Geographic Separation
geographic_separation.definition: Separating data centers geographically to deal with disasters like earthquakes or storms.

round_trip_delays.name: Round-Trip Delays
round_trip_delays.definition: Delays in communication between the browser and the application server affecting performance.

application_servers_close_geographically.name: Application Servers Close Geographically
application_servers_close_geographically.definition: Connecting users with application servers that are closest to them geographically to minimize round-trip delays.

execution_skew.name: Execution Skew
execution_skew.definition: Uneven distribution of workload among nodes in the system due to node failure.

coordinator_ci.name: Coordinator Ci
coordinator_ci.definition: The component responsible for coordinating the two-phase commit process.

participating_node_nk.name: Participating Node Nk
participating_node_nk.definition: A node involved in the two-phase commit process.

transaction_t.name: Transaction T

file.name: File

node.name: Node
node.definition: A component in the tree structure that can be locked individually.

lock_mode.name: Lock Mode
lock_mode.definition: A property of a lock that can be either shared or exclusive.

incompatible_mode.name: Incompatible Mode
incompatible_mode.definition: A property of a lock that prevents another transaction from acquiring a lock.

topic.name: Topic

topic_partition.name: Topic-Partition
topic_partition.definition: A partition of a topic in Kafka

operator.name: Operator

window_operator.name: Window Operator

stored_procedures.name: Stored Procedures

l_one.name: L1

l_k.name: Lk

disk_mirroring.name: Disk Mirroring
disk_mirroring.definition: A method where read requests can be sent to either disk in a pair.

bit_level_striping.name: Bit-Level Striping
bit_level_striping.definition: A form of data striping where bits of each byte are split across multiple disks.

block_level_striping.name: Block-Level Striping
block_level_striping.definition: A form of data striping where blocks are striped across multiple disks.

pagerank.name: PageRank
pagerank.definition: A measure of popularity of a page based on the popularity of pages that link to the page

index.name: Index Structure

lock_contention.name: Lock Contention

index_operation.name: Index Operation
index_operation.definition: An operation performed on an index structure.

serialization_order.name: Serialization Order
serialization_order.definition: An order in which operations can be executed to achieve the same result as a concurrent execution.

serializability.name: Serializability
serializability.definition: The property of a concurrent execution where the order of operations can be reordered without changing the outcome.

pr_quadtree.name: PR Quadtree
pr_quadtree.definition: A specific type of quadtree that stores points and divides space based on regions, rather than on the actual set of points stored.

region_quadtree.name: Region Quadtree
region_quadtree.definition: A quadtree used to store array (raster) information where leaf nodes represent uniform subarrays.

weak_entity_set.name: Weak Entity Set
weak_entity_set.definition: A type of entity set that must have a total participation in its identifying relationship set and can participate in relationships other than the identifying relationship.

time_slot.name: Time Slot
time_slot.definition: An entity set representing the time when a particular class section meets.

fail_stop.name: Fail-Stop Model
fail_stop.definition: A model that precludes any malicious behavior.

byzantine_consensus.name: Byzantine Consensus
byzantine_consensus.definition: A form of consensus that overcomes both the failure of a minority of nodes and possible malicious behavior of that minority.

sql_inner_join.name: Inner Join
sql_inner_join.definition: A type of join in SQL that is equivalent to a normal join.

using_join.name: Using Join

on_join.name: On Join

django_framework.name: Django Framework
django_framework.definition: A widely used web application framework for Python.

urls_py_file.name: urls.py File

person_query_view.name: person_query_view
person_query_view.definition: A view function in Django that handles the person query task.

login_view.name: login_view

authenticate_view.name: authenticate_view
authenticate_view.definition: A view function in Django that checks the login name and password.

person_query_form.name: person_query_form
person_query_form.definition: An HTML form that is displayed after successful password validation.

version_number_check.name: Version Number Check
version_number_check.definition: A check performed by Hibernate during commit processing.

conversation.name: Conversation

database_design.name: Database Design
database_design.definition: The process of designing a database, including E-R design and relational design.

course_relation.name: Course Relation
course_relation.definition: A relation in a database that includes fields like course_id, title, dept_name, credits, start, and end.

valid_time_information.name: Valid Time Information
valid_time_information.definition: Information added to a relation to track temporal changes, specifically start and end times.

sql_2011_standard.name: SQL 2011 Standard
sql_2011_standard.definition: A standard for SQL that defines how intervals should be represented.

deadlock.name: Deadlock
deadlock.definition: A situation where two or more processes are waiting on each other to release resources.

search_operation.name: Search Operation
search_operation.definition: An operation that traverses the tree structure to find specific data.

split.name: Split

coalescing.name: Coalescing
coalescing.definition: A process that merges two or more nodes into one.

redistribution.name: Redistribution
redistribution.definition: A process that reassigns data among nodes.

latch.name: Latch
latch.definition: A mechanism used to achieve mutual exclusion on shared data structures with short-held locks.

b_link_tree.name: B-Link Tree
b_link_tree.definition: A modified version of B+-trees where every node maintains a pointer to its right sibling.

index_update.name: Index Update
index_update.definition: Updating an index when a record is inserted, deleted, or updated in a file.

record_insertion.name: Record Insertion
record_insertion.definition: Inserting a new record into a file.

record_update.name: Record Update
record_update.definition: Updating a record in a file.

index_insertion.name: Index Insertion
index_insertion.definition: Inserting a new entry into an index.

index_deletion.name: Index Deletion
index_deletion.definition: Deleting an entry from an index.

transaction_t_i.name: Transaction T i

input_operation.name: Input (B X)

output_operation.definition: An operation that writes a buffer block to the disk.

locking_protocols.name: Locking Protocols

timestamp_ordering_scheme.name: Timestamp Ordering Scheme
timestamp_ordering_scheme.definition: A method for determining the serializability order among transactions in advance.

orc_file_format.name: ORC File Format
orc_file_format.definition: A columnar file representation used in big-data processing applications.

stripe.name: Stripe

row_data_area.name: Row Data Area
row_data_area.definition: Stores a compressed representation of the sequence of values for each column in an ORC file.

index_data_region.definition: Stores the starting points within a stripe for each group of values of an attribute.

query_evaluation_plan.name: Query Evaluation Plan
query_evaluation_plan.definition: A plan constructed by the system to minimize the cost of query evaluation.

query_optimization.name: Query Optimization
query_optimization.definition: The task of constructing a query-evaluation plan that minimizes the cost of query evaluation.

query_plan.name: Query Plan
query_plan.definition: The plan chosen for evaluating a query after optimization.

query_processing.name: Query Processing

query_optimizer.name: Query Optimizer

relational_algebra_representation.definition: A representation used by some databases for processing queries.

annotated_parse_tree_representation.name: Annotated Parse Tree Representation
annotated_parse_tree_representation.definition: A representation used by some databases for processing SQL queries.

data_cleansing.name: Data Cleansing
data_cleansing.definition: The task of correcting and preprocessing data.

fuzzy_lookup.name: Fuzzy Lookup

replicated_state_machines.name: Replicated State Machines
replicated_state_machines.definition: Can be used to make services, such as data storage systems and lock managers, fault tolerant.

sql_evaluation.name: SQL Evaluation

raid_5.name: RAID 5

evaluation_primitive.name: Evaluation Primitive

query_execution_plan.name: Query-Execution Plan
query_execution_plan.definition: A sequence of primitive operations that can be used to evaluate a query.

majorityofnodes.name: majority of nodes

appendentriesmessage.name: AppendEntries message

setstring.name: setString() Method

attribute_closure.name: Attribute Closure

superkey.name: Superkey

sql_standard.name: SQL Standard

host_language.name: Host Language

concurrency_control_manager.name: Concurrency Control Manager
concurrency_control_manager.definition: A part of the database system responsible for managing interactions among concurrent transactions.

takes_relationship_set.name: Takes Relationship Set
takes_relationship_set.definition: A relationship set used to model the situation where a student takes a (section of a) course.

registration_entity_set.name: Registration Entity Set
registration_entity_set.definition: An entity set representing course-registration records.

section_reg_relationship_set.name: Section Registration Relationship Set
section_reg_relationship_set.definition: A relationship set relating registration and course.

student_reg_relationship_set.name: Student Registration Relationship Set
student_reg_relationship_set.definition: A relationship set relating registration and student.

multivalued_dependency.name: Multivalued Dependency
multivalued_dependency.definition: A type of dependency that requires certain tuples to be present in the relation based on the values of other attributes.

equality_generating_dependency.name: Equality-Generating Dependency
equality_generating_dependency.definition: A term used to describe functional dependencies.

tuple_generating_dependency.name: Tuple-Generating Dependency
tuple_generating_dependency.definition: A term used to describe multivalued dependencies.

relation_schema.name: Relation Schema
relation_schema.definition: A description of the structure of a relation, including the set of attributes.

alpha_beta_subset.name: α ⊆ R and β ⊆ R
alpha_beta_subset.definition: α and β are subsets of the set of attributes R.

trivial_multivalued_dependency.name: Trivial Multivalued Dependency
trivial_multivalued_dependency.definition: A multivalued dependency that is always satisfied by all relations on schema R.

set_of_all_documents_containing_keywords.name: Set of All Documents Containing Keywords
set_of_all_documents_containing_keywords.definition: The set of all documents that contain the keywords in a query.

information_retrieval_systems.name: Information Retrieval Systems
information_retrieval_systems.definition: Systems that estimate relevance of documents to a query.

relevance_ranking.name: Relevance Ranking
relevance_ranking.definition: The process of estimating relevance of documents to a query.

checkpoint_log_record.name: Checkpoint Log Record
checkpoint_log_record.definition: A component that contains log records of transactions.

fuzzy_checkpoint.name: Fuzzy Checkpoint
fuzzy_checkpoint.definition: A type of checkpoint where transactions are allowed to perform updates while buffer blocks are being written out.

equivalence_rule.name: Equivalence Rule
equivalence_rule.definition: A rule that specifies how to transform an expression into a logically equivalent one.

cost_estimation.name: Cost Estimation
cost_estimation.definition: The process of estimating the cost of each evaluation plan using statistical information about the relations.

statistical_information.name: Statistical Information
statistical_information.definition: Information about the relations such as relation sizes and index depths used in cost estimation.

deletion_entry.name: Deletion Entry
deletion_entry.definition: A component that indicates which index entry is to be deleted.

normal_index_entry.name: Normal Index Entry
normal_index_entry.definition: A regular index entry that can be inserted and looked up.

update_entry.name: Update Entry
update_entry.definition: A component that indicates the latest value of an entry.

naive_bayesian_classifier.name: Naive Bayesian Classifier
naive_bayesian_classifier.definition: A type of probabilistic classifier that assumes attributes have independent distributions.

bayesian_classifier.name: Bayesian Classifier
bayesian_classifier.definition: A type of classifier that estimates the probability of an instance belonging to a class based on the product of the probabilities of its attribute values.

training_set.name: Training Set
training_set.definition: A set of instances used to find the distribution of attribute values for each class.

attribute_distribution.name: Attribute Distribution
attribute_distribution.definition: The distribution of values for each attribute within a specific class.

embedded_charts.name: Embedded Charts
embedded_charts.definition: Charts that can be included within text documents.

data_visualization_systems.name: Data Visualization Systems
data_visualization_systems.definition: Systems that help users examine large volumes of data and detect patterns visually.

maps.name: Maps
maps.definition: Graphical representations used to encode data such as patient locations.

charts.name: Charts
charts.definition: Graphical representations of data that can be embedded within text documents.

database_queries.name: Database Queries
database_queries.definition: Queries executed against the database to generate initial data for charts.

join_order.name: Join Order
join_order.definition: The sequence in which tables are joined in a SQL query.

cost_based_join_order_selection.name: Cost-Based Join-Order Selection
cost_based_join_order_selection.definition: A method for determining the optimal join order for a SQL query based on cost estimation.

join_predicate.name: Join Predicate
join_predicate.definition: A condition used to specify how two relations should be joined in a SQL query.

selection.name: Selection
selection.definition: A condition used to filter rows in a SQL query.

equivalent_expression.name: Equivalent Expression
equivalent_expression.definition: An alternative way of expressing a SQL query that results in the same output.

exercise_16_12.name: Exercise 16.12
exercise_16_12.definition: An exercise requiring the computation of the number of different join orders for a given number of relations.

conflicting_updates.name: Conflicting Updates
conflicting_updates.definition: Updates on the same data item that occur simultaneously and need to be resolved.

reconciliation.name: Reconciliation
reconciliation.definition: Resolution of conflicting updates to create a single common version of a data item.

shopping_cart_operations.name: Shopping Cart Operations
shopping_cart_operations.definition: Operations such as adding or deleting items from a shopping cart.

colocation.name: Colocation Technique
colocation.definition: A simple technique to handle situations by allowing multiple copies of a relation, partitioned on different attributes.

tuple_update.name: Tuple Update
tuple_update.definition: When tuples in the relation are updated, so are the copies, to keep them consistent.

student_partitions.name: Student Partitions
student_partitions.definition: Partitions of the relation based on the ID attribute.

section_relation.name: Section Relation
section_relation.definition: A relation partitioned on (course_id, year, semester, sec_id) to be colocated with the section relation.

testing_programs.name: Testing Programs
testing_programs.definition: Designing a test suite, which is a collection of test cases, to check the correctness of programs.

test_suite.name: Test Suite
test_suite.definition: A collection of test cases used to test programs.

test_cases.name: Test Cases
test_cases.definition: Individual test cases within a test suite.

program_regression.name: Program Regression
program_regression.definition: Bugs that appear due to unintended consequences of changes in the program.

regression_testing.name: Regression Testing
regression_testing.definition: Running the program on each test case in a test suite to check that the program generates the expected test output.

database_state.name: Database State
database_state.definition: The current state of the database at a given point in time.

input_to_specific_interface.name: Input to Specific Interface
input_to_specific_interface.definition: An input provided to a specific interface of the application.

sql_queries.name: SQL Queries
sql_queries.definition: Queries written in Structured Query Language used in database applications.

mutations.name: Mutations
mutations.definition: Small changes to a query (or program) that can introduce errors.

bitmap_index.name: Bitmap Index
bitmap_index.definition: A data structure where each bit in a bitmap represents a record.

existence_bitmap.name: Existence Bitmap
existence_bitmap.definition: A bitmap used to indicate whether a record exists or not.

sql_injection.name: SQL Injection
sql_injection.definition: A technique used by malicious hackers to steal data or damage the database.

building_attribute.name: Building Attribute
building_attribute.definition: An attribute in the department relation with a character string of maximum length 15.

budget_attribute.name: Budget Attribute
budget_attribute.definition: An attribute in the department relation with a number with 12 digits in total, two of which are after the decimal point.

primary_key_specification.name: Primary Key Specification
primary_key_specification.definition: A specification that attributes form the primary key for the relation, requiring non-null and unique values.

buffer_space_needed.name: Buffer Space Needed
buffer_space_needed.definition: Space required in the buffer for another block.

block_written_out.name: Block Written Out
block_written_out.definition: A block that has already been written out to disk.

pinned_block.name: Pinned Block
pinned_block.definition: A block that is currently pinned and cannot be evicted.

database_recovery.name: Database Recovery
database_recovery.definition: The process of recovering from crashes in the database system.

updated_block.name: Updated Block
updated_block.definition: A block that has been updated and needs to be written back to disk.

dept_name_budget_fd.name: dept_name → budget
dept_name_budget_fd.definition: A specific functional dependency where the attribute dept_name determines the attribute budget.

r.name: r
r.definition: A relation schema with an unspecified set of attributes R.

instance_of_relation_r.name: Instance of Relation r
instance_of_relation_r.definition: A specific instance of the relation r as depicted in Figure 7.4.

extract_transform_load_tasks.name: Extract, Transform, and Load (ETL) Tasks
extract_transform_load_tasks.definition: Steps of collecting data, cleaning/deduplicating the data, and loading the data into a warehouse.

nonrelational_sources.name: Nonrelational Sources
nonrelational_sources.definition: Sources of data where schema unification is not possible.

sequential_file_organization.name: Sequential File Organization
sequential_file_organization.definition: A method of organizing records in files where pointers are adjusted to chain records in search-key order.

cast_expression.name: Cast Expression
cast_expression.definition: An expression of the form cast(e as t) used to convert an expression e to the type t.

varchar_5.name: Varchar(5)
varchar_5.definition: A string data type with a maximum length of 5 characters.

numeric_5.name: Numeric(5)
numeric_5.definition: A numeric data type with a precision of 5 digits.

to_char_function.name: TO_CHAR Function
to_char_function.definition: A formatting function offered by Oracle and PostgreSQL.

to_number_function.name: TO_NUMBER Function
to_number_function.definition: A formatting function offered by Oracle and PostgreSQL.

to_date_function.name: TO_DATE Function
to_date_function.definition: A formatting function offered by Oracle and PostgreSQL.

convert_function.name: Convert Function
convert_function.definition: A formatting function offered by SQL Server.

distributed_file.name: Distributed File System
distributed_file.definition: A system used for parallelizing file input and output across multiple machines.

hadoop_file.name: Hadoop File System (HDFS)
hadoop_file.definition: A specific type of distributed file system discussed in Section 21.6.

parallel_distributed_storage.name: Parallel/Distributed Storage System
parallel_distributed_storage.definition: A system used for parallelizing file input and output across multiple machines.

map_reduce_operations.name: Map and Reduce Operations
map_reduce_operations.definition: Parallelized operations that are conceptually similar to relational operations project and aggregation.

workers.name: Workers
workers.definition: Processes that execute map and reduce functions on each node in the system.

tasks.name: Tasks
tasks.definition: The job of processing one piece of split input data in a MapReduce job.

nested_subquery.name: Nested Subquery
nested_subquery.definition: A select-from-where expression that is nested within another query.

set_membership_test.name: Set Membership Test
set_membership_test.definition: A common use of subqueries to test for set membership.

set_comparison.name: Set Comparison
set_comparison.definition: A common use of subqueries to make set comparisons.

set_cardinality.name: Set Cardinality
set_cardinality.definition: A common use of subqueries to determine set cardinality.

scalar_subquery.name: Scalar Subquery
scalar_subquery.definition: A class of subqueries that can appear wherever an expression returning a value can occur.

closing_connection_returns_connection_to.name: Closing Connection Returns Connection to Pool
closing_connection_returns_connection_to.definition: Closing the connection returns the connection to the pool.

caching_results_of_earlier_queries.name: Caching Results of Earlier Queries
caching_results_of_earlier_queries.definition: Caching the results of earlier queries and reusing them, so long as the query result has not changed at the database.

query_result_caching.name: Query Result Caching
query_result_caching.definition: Caching the results of earlier queries and reusing them, so long as the query result has not changed at the database.

caching_final_web_page.name: Caching Final Web Page
caching_final_web_page.definition: Caching the final web page that is sent in response to a request.

database_data_change.name: Database Data Change
database_data_change.definition: If the underlying database data change, the cached results must be discarded, or recomputed, or even incrementally updated.

query_notification.name: Query Notification
query_notification.definition: A way for the application server to register a query with the database and get a notification from the database when the result of the query changes.

version_vector_scheme.name: Version Vector Scheme
version_vector_scheme.definition: A scheme where each node stores a version vector with its copy of each data item, allowing detection of inconsistencies when replicas of a data item are independently updated.

invalidation_reports.name: Invalidation Reports
invalidation_reports.definition: Reports sent to a node upon reconnection to inform it of out-of-date cache entries.

parallel.name: Parallel Algorithm
parallel.definition: A type of algorithm designed for shared-nothing architectures.

thread.name: Thread
thread.definition: An execution stream that shares its entire memory with other threads.

bulk_synchronous_processing_framework.name: Bulk Synchronous Processing Framework
bulk_synchronous_processing_framework.definition: A framework for graph algorithms that frames them as computations associated with vertices operating in an iterative manner.

graph_database.name: Graph Database
graph_database.definition: A database management system designed to handle graph data.

superstep.name: Superstep
superstep.definition: An iteration in the Bulk Synchronous Processing framework where the method associated with each node is executed.

word_count_application.name: Word Count Application
word_count_application.definition: An application that takes a large number of files as input and outputs a count of the number of times each word appears across all the files.

mapreduce_paradigm.name: MapReduce Paradigm
mapreduce_paradigm.definition: A programming model for processing and generating big data sets with a parallel, distributed algorithm on a cluster.

sequential.name: Sequential Algorithm
sequential.definition: A straightforward algorithm that reads in the words in a file and maintains an in-memory data structure to keep track of all the words encountered so far, along with their counts.

parallel_program.name: Parallel Program
parallel_program.definition: A program that runs across many machines, with each machine processing a part of the files.

multitable_clustering.name: Multitable Clustering
multitable_clustering.definition: When multitable clustering is to be used depends on the types of queries that the database designer believes to be most frequent.

oracle_database.name: Oracle Database System
oracle_database.definition: Oracle database system supports multitable clustering.

create_cluster_command.name: Create Cluster Command
create_cluster_command.definition: A create cluster command is used to create clusters.

cluster_key.name: Cluster Key
cluster_key.definition: A specified cluster key is used in creating clusters.

cluster.name: Cluster
cluster.definition: Clusters can be created and multiple relations can be allocated to a cluster.

odbc_standard.name: ODBC Standard
odbc_standard.definition: A standard that defines an API for applications to interact with databases.

sql_environment.name: SQL Environment
sql_environment.definition: An environment created by allocating resources for ODBC operations.

database_connection_handle.name: Database Connection Handle
database_connection_handle.definition: A handle used to manage the connection between the client program and the database server.

henv_type.name: HENV Type
henv_type.definition: A type defined by ODBC for SQL environments.

hdbc_type.name: HDBC Type
hdbc_type.definition: A type defined by ODBC for database connection handles.

retnode_type.name: RETCODE Type
retnode_type.definition: A type defined by ODBC for return codes.

mobile_application.name: Mobile Application
mobile_application.definition: An application designed for mobile devices.

small_screen.name: Small Screen
small_screen.definition: A characteristic of mobile devices with limited display area.

application_code.name: Application Code
application_code.definition: Code that can be relatively large and is downloaded or updated on mobile devices.

high_speed_network.name: High-Speed Network
high_speed_network.definition: A network with fast data transfer rates, used for downloading or updating application code.

web_front_end.name: Web Front End
web_front_end.definition: The user-facing part of a web application, often implemented using JavaScript.

javascript_code.name: JavaScript Code
javascript_code.definition: Code used in web front ends to provide interactive features.

back_end.name: Back End
back_end.definition: The server-side component of an application that provides services to the front end.

api.name: API
api.definition: An interface that allows the front end to interact with the back end.

multiple_front_ends.name: Multiple Front Ends
multiple_front_ends.definition: The capability of a back end to support different types of front ends.

parallel_query_plan_space.name: Parallel Query Plan Space
parallel_query_plan_space.definition: The space of alternatives the optimizer considers when optimizing queries for parallel execution.

dense_index.name: Dense Index
dense_index.definition: An index where every search-key value has an index entry.

sparse_index.name: Sparse Index
sparse_index.definition: An index where an entry is stored for each block, and new entries are added based on search-key order.

search_key_value.name: Search Key Value
search_key_value.definition: A value used to look up records in an index.

index_entry.name: Index Entry
index_entry.definition: A structure in the index that contains information about records.

schedule_1.name: Schedule 1
schedule_1.definition: A schedule showing the actions executed by the transactions and the points at which the concurrency-control manager grants the locks.

transaction_t2.name: Transaction T2
transaction_t2.definition: A transaction that displays the value $300 if executed serially after T1, but $250 if executed concurrently with T1.

lock_request.name: Lock Request
lock_request.definition: A request made by a transaction to the concurrency-control manager for a lock on a data item.

top_n_results.name: Top N Results
top_n_results.definition: A query that returns the top N results without using the rank function.

bottom_n.name: Bottom N
bottom_n.definition: A concept similar to Top N but with a reverse sorting order.

rank_function.name: Rank Function
rank_function.definition: A function used to determine the rank of tuples in a partition.

percent_rank.name: Percent Rank
percent_rank.definition: A function that gives the rank of a tuple as a fraction.

cume_dist.name: Cumulative Distribution
cume_dist.definition: A function that calculates the cumulative distribution for a tuple.

analysis_pass.name: Analysis Pass
analysis_pass.definition: A pass in the ARIES recovery algorithm that determines which transactions to undo, which pages were dirty at the time of the crash, and the LSN from which the redo pass should start.

undo_pass.name: Undo Pass
undo_pass.definition: A pass in the ARIES recovery algorithm that rolls back all transactions that were incomplete at the time of crash.

light_node.name: Light Node
light_node.definition: A node that does not store the entire blockchain but retains only the root hash of the Merkle tree for verification.

full_node.name: Full Node
full_node.definition: A node that stores the entire blockchain and can provide any needed data to a light node.

information_retrieval.name: Information Retrieval
information_retrieval.definition: The querying of unstructured textual data.

document.name: Document
document.definition: A collection of textual information, such as a database text-valued attribute or a web page.

node_dn.name: Distinguished Name of a Node
node_dn.definition: A distinguished name that contains all the RDNs of the parent node and one or more additional RDNs.

rdn_value.name: RDN Value
rdn_value.definition: The value of a Relative Distinguished Name, which is used to construct the full distinguished name.

dit.name: Directory Information Tree
dit.definition: A hierarchical structure where each node has a distinguished name that includes the RDNs of its parent and additional RDNs.

alias_entry.name: Alias Entry
alias_entry.definition: An entry at the leaf level of a DIT that acts as an alias pointing to an entry in another branch of the tree.

block_nested_loop_join.name: Block Nested-Loop Join
block_nested_loop_join.definition: A variant of the nested-loop join where every block of the inner relation is paired with every block of the outer relation.

two_kinds_of_locks.name: Two Kinds of Locks
two_kinds_of_locks.definition: Shared locks for read operations and exclusive locks for write operations.

commit_log_record.name: Commit Log Record
commit_log_record.definition: The last log record of a transaction.

atomic_domain.name: Atomic Domain
atomic_domain.definition: A domain is atomic if elements of the domain are considered to be indivisible units.

phone_number_attribute.name: Phone Number Attribute
phone_number_attribute.definition: An attribute in a relational database that stores a phone number.

dense_rank_function.name: Dense Rank Function
dense_rank_function.definition: A function that assigns ranks without creating gaps in the ordering.

gpa.name: GPA
gpa.definition: An attribute used in ranking students based on their grades.

null_values.name: Null Values
null_values.definition: Values that are missing or undefined.

l_0_tree.name: L0 Tree
l_0_tree.definition: A specific type of LSM tree used in memory.

sql_window_operations.name: SQL Window Operations
sql_window_operations.definition: Described in Section 5.5.2, these are window functions supported by SQL.

stream_query_languages.name: Stream Query Languages
stream_query_languages.definition: Supports additional window types beyond what SQL window functions provide.

tumbling_window.name: Tumbling Window
tumbling_window.definition: A type of window where non-overlapping windows are used, e.g., hourly windows.

hopping_window.name: Hopping Window
hopping_window.definition: A type of window where overlapping windows are used, e.g., hourly windows computed every 20 minutes.

sliding_window.name: Sliding Window
sliding_window.definition: A type of window where windows slide over time or tuples, e.g., windows of a specified size around each incoming tuple.

session_window.name: Session Window
session_window.definition: A type of window that models user sessions with a timeout interval.

employee_schema.name: Employee Schema
employee_schema.definition: A schema with attributes ID, name, street, city, and salary.

student_schema.name: Student Schema
student_schema.definition: A schema with attributes ID, name, street, city, and tot_cred.

person_schema.name: Person Schema
person_schema.definition: A schema containing at least the primary-key attributes of the person entity.

hypercube_interconnect.name: Hypercube Interconnect
hypercube_interconnect.definition: A type of interconnect where components are numbered in binary and connected if their binary representations differ in exactly one bit.

mesh_interconnect.name: Mesh Interconnect
mesh_interconnect.definition: A type of interconnect where components are connected in a grid, potentially requiring many links for communication.

tree_like_interconnect.name: Tree-like Interconnect
tree_like_interconnect.definition: A type of interconnect used in server systems in data centers, involving racks and network switches.

recovery_algorithms.name: Recovery Algorithms
recovery_algorithms.definition: Algorithms used to ensure database consistency and transaction atomicity despite failures.

normal_transaction_processing.name: Normal Transaction Processing
normal_transaction_processing.definition: Process during which actions are taken to ensure that enough information exists to allow recovery from failures.

failure_classification.name: Failure Classification
failure_classification.definition: Process of considering how failure modes affect the contents of the database.

database_consistency.name: Database Consistency
database_consistency.definition: State where the database is free from any type of logical inconsistencies.

transaction_atomicity.name: Transaction Atomicity
transaction_atomicity.definition: Property where each transaction appears to be indivisible and its effects are either all completed or none at all.

virtual_nodes.name: Virtual Nodes
virtual_nodes.definition: A concept where several times as many virtual nodes as real nodes are pretended to exist.

round_robin_allocation.name: Round-Robin Allocation
round_robin_allocation.definition: An algorithm that maps virtual nodes to real nodes using a round-robin method.

tuple_partitioning.name: Tuple Partitioning
tuple_partitioning.definition: A process of mapping tuples and work to virtual nodes instead of to real nodes.

load_balancing.name: Load Balancing
load_balancing.definition: A process of balancing the number of stored tuples and the load across real nodes.

raster_data.name: Raster Data
raster_data.definition: Such data consist of bitmaps or pixel maps, in two or more dimensions.

vector_data.name: Vector Data
vector_data.definition: Vector data are constructed from basic geometric objects, such as points, line segments,...

tiles.name: Tiles
tiles.definition: A component used to represent raster data, each covering a fixed-size area.

zoom_level.name: Zoom Level
zoom_level.definition: A property that allows the display of data at different resolutions.

increasing_amount_of_personal_data.name: Increasing Amount of Personal Data
increasing_amount_of_personal_data.definition: An increasing amount of personal data are available online.

privacy_of_personal_data.name: Privacy of Personal Data
privacy_of_personal_data.definition: The privacy of personal data such as medical data.

privacy_laws.name: Privacy Laws
privacy_laws.definition: Laws that define when and to whom the data may be revealed.

criminal_penalties.name: Criminal Penalties
criminal_penalties.definition: Penalties that can be imposed for violation of privacy law.

applications_accessing_private_data.name: Applications Accessing Private Data
applications_accessing_private_data.definition: Applications that access such private data.

aggregated_private_data.name: Aggregated Private Data
aggregated_private_data.definition: Aggregated private data that can play an important role in many tasks.

researchers_carrying_out_tasks.name: Researchers Carrying Out Tasks
researchers_carrying_out_tasks.definition: Researchers carrying out tasks such as detecting drug side effects or detecting the spread of epidemics.

hospital.name: Hospital
hospital.definition: A hospital that hides the name of the patient but provides other identifying information.

year_of_birth.name: Year of Birth
year_of_birth.definition: The year of birth of the patient.

postal_code.name: Postal Code
postal_code.definition: The postal code of the patient.

data_redundancy_and_inconsistency.name: Data Redundancy and Inconsistency
data_redundancy_and_inconsistency.definition: When the same information is duplicated in several places, leading to higher storage and access costs and potential data inconsistency.

page_6.name: Page 6
page_6.definition: A reference to a specific page in the document.

file_processing.name: File Processing System
file_processing.definition: A system where organizational information is stored in separate files created by different programmers over time.

student_records.name: Student Records
student_records.definition: Structured data containing information about students, possibly organized by department.

postal_code_area.name: Postal Code Area
postal_code_area.definition: A geographical area defined by postal codes.

credit_hours.name: Credit Hours
credit_hours.definition: A measure of the amount of work required for a course or program.

composite_attribute.name: Composite Attribute
composite_attribute.definition: An attribute that consists of multiple component attributes.

multivalued_attribute.name: Multivalued Attribute
multivalued_attribute.definition: An attribute that can have multiple values for a single entity.

derived_attribute.name: Derived Attribute
derived_attribute.definition: An attribute that is not explicitly represented in the relational data model but can be represented in other data models using stored procedures, functions, or methods.

address_attribute.name: Address Attribute
address_attribute.definition: A composite attribute that includes street, city, state, and postal code.

street_attribute.name: Street Attribute
street_attribute.definition: A composite attribute that is further decomposed into street number, street name, and apartment number.

disk_platter.name: Disk Platter
disk_platter.definition: A rigid metal or glass platter in a magnetic disk, with two surfaces covered in magnetic material for storing information.

read_write_head.name: Read-Write Head
read_write_head.definition: A component that moves across the surface of a platter to access different tracks and store information magnetically.

track.name: Track
track.definition: A logical division of the disk surface, subdivided into sectors, used for organizing information.

sector.name: Sector
sector.definition: The smallest unit of information that can be read from or written to the disk, typically 512 bytes.

partial_aggregation.name: Partial Aggregation
partial_aggregation.definition: A technique used to reduce skew by performing partial aggregation.

combiners.name: Combiners
combiners.definition: Components in the MapReduce framework that correspond to partial aggregation.

mapreduce.name: MapReduce
mapreduce.definition: A framework for implementing distributed data processing tasks.

projection.name: Projection
projection.definition: An operation that selects specific columns from a relation.

set_difference.name: Set Difference
set_difference.definition: An operation that returns elements present in one set but not in another.

linear_search.name: Linear Search
linear_search.definition: A process of searching through data by examining each element one by one.

bitmap_index_scan.name: Bitmap Index Scan Algorithm
bitmap_index_scan.definition: An algorithm used by PostgreSQL to handle situations where the number of matching records is not known precisely.

wide_column_store.name: Wide Column Store
wide_column_store.definition: A type of key-value store that allows columns to be added to, or deleted from, individual tuples.

document_store.name: Document Store
document_store.definition: A type of key-value store that allows the value stored with a key to have a complex structure, typically based on JSON.

parallel_key_value_store.name: Parallel Key-Value Store
parallel_key_value_store.definition: A type of key-value store that supports elasticity, allowing the number of nodes to be increased or decreased incrementally.

commit_processing.name: Commit Processing
