limiting_factor.name: Limiting Factor
limiting_factor.definition: The speed at which random data can be accessed, limited by the disk arm movement speed.

i_o_operations_per_transaction.name: I/O Operations Per Transaction
i_o_operations_per_transaction.definition: The number of input/output operations performed during a single transaction.

memory.name: Memory
memory.definition: A component where data is stored to reduce disk I/O operations.

disk.name: Disk
disk.definition: A storage device with limited access speed, often used for data storage.

page_access_frequency.name: Page Access Frequency
page_access_frequency.definition: How frequently a specific page is accessed within a certain time frame.

rdd_partitioning.name: RDD Partitioning
rdd_partitioning.definition: RDDs may be partitioned and stored on multiple machines.

reducebykey.name: reduceByKey
reducebykey.definition: reduceByKey() would repartition the input RDD to bring all records belonging to a group together on a single machine.

textfile_operation.name: textFile() Operation
textfile_operation.definition: The leaf operation textFile() reads data from a file.

flatmap_operation.name: flatMap() Operation
flatmap_operation.definition: The next operation flatMap() has the textFile() operation as its child.

maptopairs_operation.name: mapToPairs() Operation
maptopairs_operation.definition: The mapToPairs() in turn has flatMap() as child.

centralized_databases.name: Centralized Databases
centralized_databases.definition: Databases where all data is stored in a single location.

parallel_databases.name: Parallel Databases
parallel_databases.definition: Databases where data is distributed across multiple nodes.

view_maintenance.name: View Maintenance
view_maintenance.definition: Updating materialized views when the database is updated.

subquery_expression.name: Subquery Expression
subquery_expression.definition: Any select-from-where expression that returns a relation as a result.

select_from_where_expression.name: Select-From-Where Expression
select_from_where_expression.definition: An expression that selects from a relation with a specified where condition.

outer_query.name: Outer Query
outer_query.definition: The main query that uses the results of a subquery.

subquery_result_relation.name: Subquery Result Relation
subquery_result_relation.definition: The relation generated by a subquery that can be used in an outer query.

linear_probing.name: Linear Probing
linear_probing.definition: A policy where records are inserted into the next available bucket in cyclic order.

open_addressing.name: Open Addressing
open_addressing.definition: A method of handling collisions by searching alternative locations within the same table.

closed_addressing.name: Closed Addressing
closed_addressing.definition: A method of handling collisions by using a separate overflow area or chaining.

bucket_overflow.name: Bucket Overflow
bucket_overflow.definition: A condition where a bucket contains more records than it can hold.

slotted_page.name: Slotted Page Structure
slotted_page.definition: A method of storing records in a block where records may move within a block as other records are deleted or resized.

buffer.name: Buffer
buffer.definition: A component in main-memory databases used for loading and evicting records.

direct_allocation.name: Direct Allocation
direct_allocation.definition: A method of allocating records in main memory without using a slotted-page structure.

memory_fragmentation.name: Memory Fragmentation
memory_fragmentation.definition: A situation where memory becomes divided into small unusable pieces due to repeated insertion and deletion of variable-sized records.

distinct_keyword.name: DISTINCT Keyword
distinct_keyword.definition: An SQL keyword used to eliminate duplicates in the results of a query.

computer_science_department.name: Computer Science Department
computer_science_department.definition: A specific department within the instructor relation.

bestplan.name: Best Plan
bestplan.definition: The best way of accessing S, taking selections on S into account.

table_r.name: Table r
table_r.definition: A table used in the join operation to create the materialized view.

table_s.name: Table s
table_s.definition: A table used in the join operation to create the materialized view.

inserts_i_r.name: Inserts i_r
inserts_i_r.definition: A set of tuples inserted into table r.

deletes_d_r.name: Deletes d_r
deletes_d_r.definition: A set of tuples deleted from table r.

transaction_coordinator_sub.name: Transaction Coordinator Subsystem
transaction_coordinator_sub.definition: A subsystem responsible for coordinating the execution of all transactions initiated at that node.

single_valued_attribute.name: Single Valued Attribute
single_valued_attribute.definition: An attribute that has only one value for a specific entity.

base_attribute.name: Base Attribute
base_attribute.definition: An attribute whose value is stored and used to derive the value of a derived attribute.

stored_attribute.name: Stored Attribute
stored_attribute.definition: An attribute whose value is stored and used to derive the value of a derived attribute.

virtual_node_partitioning.name: Virtual Node Partitioning
virtual_node_partitioning.definition: A method used in parallel joins where data is partitioned into virtual nodes.

work_stealing.name: Work Stealing
work_stealing.definition: A technique where an idle processor takes work from the queue of a busy processor.

bloom_filter.name: Bloom Filter
bloom_filter.definition: A probabilistic data structure that can check for membership of a value in a set using very little space, but at a small risk of overestimating the set of elements that are in the set.

bitmap.name: Bitmap
bitmap.definition: A basic data structure used in a Bloom filter to store bits.

hash_function_h.name: Hash Function h
hash_function_h.definition: A function that computes a hash value for an element v, with the range being 1 to 10n.

independent_hash_functions_h_i.name: Independent Hash Functions h_i
independent_hash_functions_h_i.definition: k independent hash functions used in a Bloom filter, where k > 1.

index_sequential_organization.name: Index-Sequential Organization
index_sequential_organization.definition: A method of organizing files of records as ordered files.

b_plus_tree_organization.name: B+ Tree Organization
b_plus_tree_organization.definition: A method of organizing files of records using B+ trees.

heap_file.name: Heap File
heap_file.definition: A method of organizing files where records are not ordered in any particular way.

hash_file_organization.name: Hash File Organization
hash_file_organization.definition: A method of organizing files using hashing.

node_split.name: Node Split
node_split.definition: A process in B+ tree indices where nodes are split to handle relation size increases.

bucket_address_table_doubling.name: Bucket Address Table Doubling
bucket_address_table_doubling.definition: A process in extendable hashing where the bucket address table is doubled to handle relation size increases.

apache_hadoop.name: Apache Hadoop
apache_hadoop.definition: A system that can handle any kind of data, including relational data.

hive.name: Hive System
hive.definition: A system that allows SQL queries to be executed on top of the Hadoop system.

cloudera.name: Cloudera
cloudera.definition: A company that provides software to optimize Hive query processing.

hortonworks.name: Hortonworks
hortonworks.definition: A company that provides software to optimize Hive query processing.

parquet_file_format.name: Parquet File Format
parquet_file_format.definition: A compressed file structure containing records with columns used to store such log records.

two_tier_architecture.name: Two-Tier Architecture
two_tier_architecture.definition: A type of architecture where the client machine contains direct database calls.

three_tier_architecture.name: Three-Tier Architecture
three_tier_architecture.definition: A type of architecture where the client machine acts as a front end and does not contain any direct database calls, communicating with an application server which then communicates with a database system.

application_server.name: Application Server
application_server.definition: A component that communicates with a database system to access data and contains the business logic of the application.

client_machine.name: Client Machine
client_machine.definition: A component that acts as a front end in a three-tier architecture and does not contain any direct database calls.

web_browser.name: Web Browser
web_browser.definition: An application client, commonly used in modern database applications.

using_condition.name: USING Condition
using_condition.definition: A form of natural join that requires values to match only on specified attributes.

join_expression.name: Join Expression
join_expression.definition: The part of a SQL query that specifies how tables are joined together.

student_table.name: Student Table
student_table.definition: A table representing students with an ID attribute.

takes_table.name: Takes Table
takes_table.definition: A table representing enrollments with an ID attribute.

clr.name: CLR
clr.definition: A component that contains the undo action performed and the LSN of the next log record to be undone.

lsn.name: LSN
lsn.definition: A property that stands for Last Sequence Number, used to identify log records.

multiple_granularity_locking.name: Multiple Granularity Locking
multiple_granularity_locking.definition: A method where locking is applied at different levels of granularity.

data_item_locking.name: Data Item Locking
data_item_locking.definition: Locking the data item corresponding to the relation, preventing other transactions from updating information about what tuples are in the relation.

tuple_locking.name: Tuple Locking
tuple_locking.definition: Locking individual tuples, allowing transactions to access them even if another transaction has an exclusive lock on the data item.

short_transactions.name: Short Transactions
short_transactions.definition: Short transactions that access only a few data items.

long_transactions.name: Long Transactions
long_transactions.definition: Long transactions that produce reports from an entire file or set of files.

relation_scan_operations.name: Relation Scan Operations
relation_scan_operations.definition: Operations performed by a query that acquire a lock at a relation level.

index_scan_operations.name: Index Scan Operations
index_scan_operations.definition: Operations performed by a query that acquire an intention lock at the relation level and regular locks at the tuple level.

lock_table.name: Lock Table
lock_table.definition: A component used by the lock manager to keep track of locks acquired by transactions.

2pc.name: 2PC
2pc.definition: A protocol used for committing updates to replicas atomically.

database_buffer.name: Database Buffer
database_buffer.definition: A portion of main memory allocated for storing database data.

disk_i_o_operations.name: Disk I/O Operations
disk_i_o_operations.definition: Operations performed to read from or write to a disk.

main_memory_database.name: Main-Memory Database
main_memory_database.definition: A database where all data reside in memory.

record_pointer.name: Record Pointer
record_pointer.definition: A reference to a specific record in a database.

flash_memory_device.name: Flash Memory Device
flash_memory_device.definition: A type of non-volatile memory used in solid-state drives (SSDs)

tape_array.name: Tape Array
tape_array.definition: An array of tape storage devices

broadcast_data.name: Broadcast Data
broadcast_data.definition: The process of transmitting data over a network or wireless system

naive_user.name: Naïve User
naive_user.definition: Unsophisticated users who interact with the system through predefined user interfaces like web or mobile applications.

application_programmer.name: Application Programmer
application_programmer.definition: Computer professionals who write application programs and can choose from many tools to develop user interfaces.

sophisticated_user.name: Sophisticated User
sophisticated_user.definition: Users who interact with the system without writing programs, forming their requests using a database query language or data analysis software.

performance_benchmark.name: Performance Benchmark
performance_benchmark.definition: A suite of standardized tasks used to measure the performance of a system.

task.name: Task
task.definition: A specific operation or set of operations performed by a system.

system_a.name: System A
system_a.definition: A system that runs Task T1 at 99 transactions per second and Task T2 at 1 transaction per second.

system_b.name: System B
system_b.definition: A system that runs both Task T1 and Task T2 at 50 transactions per second.

long_delays_and_timeouts.name: Long Delays and Timeouts
long_delays_and_timeouts.definition: Users experienced long delays and time-outs in web applications.

high_cpu_usage.name: High CPU Usage
high_cpu_usage.definition: CPU usage was very high while disk and network usage was negligible.

full_relation_scan.name: Full Relation Scan
full_relation_scan.definition: A simple lookup query on a large relation was using a full relation scan.

bad_query_plan.name: Bad Query Plan
bad_query_plan.definition: The optimizer produced a bad plan for the query.

nested_subqueries.name: Nested Subqueries
nested_subqueries.definition: The programmer had written an unnecessarily complicated query with several nested subqueries.

joins.name: Joins
joins.definition: Rewriting the query using joins instead of nested subqueries.

decorrelated_query.name: Decorrelated Query
decorrelated_query.definition: Rewriting the query to decorrelate it.

sql_exception.name: SQL Exception
sql_exception.definition: An SQL-specific exception that arises when JDBC calls are made.

general_exception.name: General Exception
general_exception.definition: Any Java exception such as a null-pointer exception or array-index-out-of-bounds exception.

try_catch_construct.name: Try-Catch Construct
try_catch_construct.definition: A programming construct that allows catching and handling exceptions.

connection.name: Connection
connection.definition: A resource used to establish a communication link to a database.

statement.name: Statement
statement.definition: An object used to execute SQL statements on a database.

try_with_resources_construct.name: Try-With-Resources Construct
try_with_resources_construct.definition: A Java construct that automatically closes resources upon completion of the block.

failure_with_loss_of_non_volatile_storag.name: Failure with Loss of Non-Volatile Storage
failure_with_loss_of_non_volatile_storag.definition: A type of failure where the content of non-volatile storage is lost.

database_dump.name: Database Dump
database_dump.definition: The process of periodically dumping the entire contents of the database to stable storage.

magnetic_tape.name: Magnetic Tape
magnetic_tape.definition: A type of stable storage used for database dumping.

partial_failure_non_volatile_storage.name: Partial Failure of Non-Volatile Storage
partial_failure_non_volatile_storage.definition: A failure where only a single block or a few blocks of non-volatile storage fail.

archival_dump.name: Archival Dump
archival_dump.definition: A dump of the database contents that can be archived and used later to examine old states of the database.

sql_dump.name: SQL Dump
sql_dump.definition: A dump that writes out SQL DDL statements and SQL insert statements to a file, which can be re-executed to re-create the database.

fuzzy_dump_scheme.name: Fuzzy Dump Scheme
fuzzy_dump_scheme.definition: A scheme that allows transactions to be active while the dump is in progress, reducing the impact on transaction processing.

ranking.name: Ranking
ranking.definition: Finding the position of a value within a set, such as assigning students a rank in class based on their grade-point average.

find_all_prereqs_function.name: findAllPrereqs
find_all_prereqs_function.definition: A function to find all direct and indirect prerequisites of a given course.

c_pereq_table.name: c_pereq
c_pereq_table.definition: A temporary table that stores the set of tuples to be returned.

new_c_prereq_table.name: new_c_prereq
new_c_prereq_table.definition: A temporary table that stores the courses found in the previous iteration.

temp_table.name: temp
temp_table.definition: A temporary table used as temporary storage while sets of courses are manipulated.

direct_prerequisites.name: direct prerequisites
direct_prerequisites.definition: Courses that directly precede another course.

indirect_prerequisites.name: indirect prerequisites
indirect_prerequisites.definition: Courses that indirectly precede another course through a chain of direct prerequisites.

left_deep_join_trees.name: Left-Deep Join Trees
left_deep_join_trees.definition: A type of join order where a left-deep join order is considered, starting with a different one of the n relations.

heuristic.name: Heuristic Approach
heuristic.definition: An approach to reduce the cost of join-order selection by considering n evaluation plans and choosing the best one based on minimizing the number of nested-loop joins without an index and the number of sort-merge joins.

nested_loop_joins.name: Nested-Loop Joins
nested_loop_joins.definition: A type of join operation where one table is scanned for each row of another table.

sort_merge_joins.name: Sort-Merge Joins
sort_merge_joins.definition: A type of join operation where both tables are sorted on the join key and then merged.

redo_log_records.name: Redo Log Records
redo_log_records.definition: Records of updates carried out by the backup site while the old primary was down.

hot_spare_configuration.name: Hot-Spare Configuration
hot_spare_configuration.definition: A configuration where the remote backup site continually processes redo log records and is ready to process new transactions immediately after the primary fails.

single_database.name: Single Database System
single_database.definition: A single database system typically has sufficient storage and performance to handle all the transaction processing needs of an enterprise.

partitioning_attributes.name: Partitioning Attributes
partitioning_attributes.definition: Partitioning is usually done on one or more attributes, referred to as partitioning attributes, partitioning keys, or shard keys.

user_account_identifiers.name: User/Account Identifiers
user_account_identifiers.definition: User or account identifiers are commonly used as partitioning keys.

range_partitioning.name: Range Partitioning
range_partitioning.definition: Such partitioning is called range partitioning, where keys are assigned to different databases based on a range.

plan_caching.name: Plan Caching
plan_caching.definition: A technique where the plan chosen by the optimizer is cached and reused if the query is submitted again with the same constants.

parametric_query_optimization.name: Parametric Query Optimization
parametric_query_optimization.definition: An approach where a query is optimized without specific values for its parameters, resulting in multiple plans that are optimal for different parameter values.

simplified_banking.name: Simplified Banking System
simplified_banking.definition: A simplified model of a banking system used for explanation.

account_a.name: Account A
account_a.definition: An account with an initial balance of $1000.

account_b.name: Account B
account_b.definition: An account with an initial balance of $2000.

buffer_block_b_a.name: Buffer Block B A
buffer_block_b_a.definition: A buffer block on which the value of Account A resides.

buffer_block_b_b.name: Buffer Block B B
buffer_block_b_b.definition: A buffer block on which the value of Account B resides.

incremental_change_computation.name: Incremental Change Computation
incremental_change_computation.definition: Deriving expressions for computing the incremental change to the result of each subexpression.

materialized_view_e1_e2.name: Materialized View E1 ⋈ E2
materialized_view_e1_e2.definition: A materialized view resulting from the join of two subexpressions E1 and E2.

insertion_into_relation_r.name: Insertion into Relation R
insertion_into_relation_r.definition: Inserting a set of tuples into relation r.

expression_d1.name: Expression D1
expression_d1.definition: An expression representing the set of tuples to be inserted into E1.

linked_open_data_project.name: Linked Open Data Project
linked_open_data_project.definition: A project aimed at making a variety of knowledge graphs open source and creating links between them.

wikidata.name: Wikidata
wikidata.definition: A knowledge base that provides an RDF/knowledge graph representation of a wide variety of knowledge.

dbpedia.name: DBPedia
dbpedia.definition: A knowledge base that provides an RDF/knowledge graph representation of a wide variety of knowledge.

freebase.name: Freebase
freebase.definition: A knowledge base that provides an RDF/knowledge graph representation of a wide variety of knowledge.

yago.name: Yago
yago.definition: A knowledge base that provides an RDF/knowledge graph representation of a wide variety of knowledge.

intra_node_partitioning.name: Intra-Node Partitioning
intra_node_partitioning.definition: A method of partitioning a relation where frequently accessed tuples are stored separately from infrequently accessed tuples.

horizontal_partitioning_across_nodes.name: Horizontal Partitioning Across Nodes
horizontal_partitioning_across_nodes.definition: A method of partitioning a relation across multiple nodes.

local_wait_for_graph.name: Local Wait-For Graph
local_wait_for_graph.definition: A graph constructed for local transactions and data items.

global_wait_for_graph.name: Global Wait-For Graph
global_wait_for_graph.definition: A graph constructed as the union of all local wait-for graphs maintained in a single node.

transaction_t3.name: Transaction T3
transaction_t3.definition: A transaction that has requested items at both nodes.

node_n1.name: Node N1
node_n1.definition: A node in the distributed database system.

node_n2.name: Node N2
node_n2.definition: A node in the distributed database system.

reflexivity_rule.name: Reflexivity Rule
reflexivity_rule.definition: A rule stating that α → α always holds.

transitivity_rule.name: Transitivity Rule
transitivity_rule.definition: A rule stating that if α → β and β → γ, then α → γ.

union_rule.name: Union Rule
union_rule.definition: A rule stating that if α → β and α → γ, then α → β ∪ γ.

repeat_loop.name: Repeat Loop
repeat_loop.definition: A process where attributes are added to result based on certain conditions.

result_set.name: Result Set
result_set.definition: A set of attributes that are being updated during the execution of the algorithm.

attribute_a.name: Attribute A
attribute_a.definition: An attribute in α+ that is not yet in result during the execution of the algorithm.

course_entity_set.name: Course Entity Set
course_entity_set.definition: An entity set containing attributes like course_id, title, dept_name, and credits.

id_attribute.name: ID Attribute
id_attribute.definition: An attribute used to uniquely identify entities within an entity set.

delete_operation.name: Delete Operation
delete_operation.definition: An operation that removes a data item.

timestamp_ordering_protocol.name: Timestamp Ordering Protocol
timestamp_ordering_protocol.definition: A concurrency control protocol where a transaction sets timestamps for a newly inserted data item.

ldap_protocol.name: LDAP Protocol
ldap_protocol.definition: A widely used protocol for accessing directory information.

jdbc_protocol.name: JDBC Protocol
jdbc_protocol.definition: A protocol for accessing data in a database system.

odbc_protocol.name: ODBC Protocol
odbc_protocol.definition: A protocol for accessing data in a database system.

directory_access_protocols.name: Directory Access Protocols
directory_access_protocols.definition: Standardized ways of accessing data in a directory.

lightweight_directory_access_protocol.name: Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP)
lightweight_directory_access_protocol.definition: The most widely used protocol for accessing directory information.

distributed_directory.name: Distributed Directory System
distributed_directory.definition: A system where directory information is stored across multiple directory servers.

update_transaction.name: Update Transaction
update_transaction.definition: A transaction that attempts to modify data in a database.

first_updater.name: First Updater
first_updater.definition: The initial transaction that attempts to update data.

subsequent_updater.name: Subsequent Updater
subsequent_updater.definition: A transaction that attempts to update data after the first updater.

write_lock.name: Write Lock
write_lock.definition: A type of lock that prevents other transactions from modifying the locked data.

transaction_timestamp.name: Transaction Timestamp
transaction_timestamp.definition: A timestamp assigned to each transaction when it begins.

read_timestamp.name: Read Timestamp
read_timestamp.definition: The largest timestamp of those transactions that have read a particular data item.

write_timestamp.name: Write Timestamp
write_timestamp.definition: The timestamp of the transaction that wrote the current value of a data item.

sorting.name: Sorting
sorting.definition: The process of arranging data in a particular order.

logical_sorting.name: Logical Sorting
logical_sorting.definition: Sorting that orders the relation through an index rather than physically.

physical_sorting.name: Physical Sorting
physical_sorting.definition: Sorting that orders the records directly without the need for an index.

quick_sort.name: Quick-Sort
quick_sort.definition: A standard sorting technique that uses a divide-and-conquer approach.

disconnected_node.name: Disconnected Node
disconnected_node.definition: A node running an application that is disconnected from other nodes.

replicated_data.name: Replicated Data
replicated_data.definition: Data that are copied across multiple nodes for redundancy and availability.

partitioned_network.name: Partitioned Network
partitioned_network.definition: A network where nodes are split into separate groups, unable to communicate with each other.

storage.name: Storage System
storage.definition: A system that stores data and can be accessed by nodes.

mobile_device.name: Mobile Device
mobile_device.definition: A device that can operate independently of a network connection.

generalized_search_tree_gist.name: GiST
generalized_search_tree_gist.definition: A type of index structure in PostgreSQL that allows user-defined code.

total_failure.name: Total Failure
total_failure.definition: A failure that occurred sufficiently early during the transfer that the destination block remains intact.

recovery_procedure.name: Recovery Procedure
recovery_procedure.definition: A procedure invoked by the system to restore a block to a consistent state after a data-transfer failure.

physical_block.name: Physical Block
physical_block.definition: A component used in the stable-storage implementation, which can be either local or remote.

logical_database_block.name: Logical Database Block
logical_database_block.definition: A component of the database that is represented by two physical blocks in the stable-storage implementation.

checksum.name: Checksum
checksum.definition: A property used to detect errors in a disk block, such as a partial write to the block.

flash_storage.name: Flash Storage
flash_storage.definition: A type of storage that uses flash memory technology, replacing magnetic disks in many applications.

ssd_storage.name: SSD Storage
ssd_storage.definition: Solid-state drive storage that uses flash memory, providing faster random I/O operations than magnetic disks.

magnetic_disk_storage.name: Magnetic Disk Storage
magnetic_disk_storage.definition: Traditional storage using magnetic disks, which are being replaced by flash-based SSD storage in many applications.

page.name: Page
page.definition: A unit of data storage in flash memory, typically used in the context of B+ tree indices.

version_number.name: Version Number
version_number.definition: A number incremented each time the data item is updated.

test_and_set_function.name: Test-and-Set Function
test_and_set_function.definition: A function that allows an update to a data item to be conditional on the current version of the data item being the same as a specified version number.

data_item.name: Data Item
data_item.definition: A component in a distributed database that can be updated and has a version number.

ldap.name: LDAP
ldap.definition: A lightweight directory access protocol that provides many of the X.500 features but with less complexity.

x_500_directory_access_protocol.name: X.500 Directory Access Protocol
x_500_directory_access_protocol.definition: A standard for accessing directory information defined by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO).

active_directory.name: Microsoft Active Directory
active_directory.definition: A directory system based on LDAP used in a large number of organizations.

read_one_write_all_copies_protocol.name: Read One, Write All Copies Protocol
read_one_write_all_copies_protocol.definition: A protocol where writes must be successfully performed at all replicas of a data item, and reads may read from any replica.

read_one_write_all_available_protocol.name: Read One, Write All Available Protocol
read_one_write_all_available_protocol.definition: A protocol where reads proceed as in the read one, write all scheme, and a write operation is shipped to all replicas, acquiring write locks on all the replicas.

internal_organization.name: Internal Organization Structure
internal_organization.definition: The complex internal organization structure of large organizations where different data may be present in different locations, on different operational systems, or under different schemas.

record_transaction_i_operation_abort.name: Record <T_i, O_j, operation-abort>
record_transaction_i_operation_abort.definition: A log record indicating the operation-abort event.

record_transaction_i_operation_begin.name: Record <T_i, O_j, operation-begin>
record_transaction_i_operation_begin.definition: A log record indicating the beginning of an operation.

record_transaction_i_start.name: Record <T_i start>
record_transaction_i_start.definition: A log record indicating the start of a transaction.

record_transaction_i_abort.name: Record <T_i abort>
record_transaction_i_abort.definition: A log record indicating the abort of a transaction.

physical_log_records.name: Physical Log Records
physical_log_records.definition: Log records containing old values used for rolling back operations.

weak_consistency_protocol.name: Weak Consistency Protocol
weak_consistency_protocol.definition: A protocol that only guarantees weak consistency.

malicious_user.name: Malicious User
malicious_user.definition: A user who does not have the private key used for signing the value and can modify the contents.

query_processing_algorithms.name: Query Processing Algorithms
query_processing_algorithms.definition: Algorithms that focus on minimizing I/O cost.

cache_conscious_query_processing_algorit.name: Cache-Conscious Query Processing Algorithms
cache_conscious_query_processing_algorit.definition: Algorithms that help minimize memory access costs.

query_compilation.name: Query Compilation
query_compilation.definition: Techniques used in query processing to minimize memory access costs.

advisor_relation.name: Advisor Relation
advisor_relation.definition: A relation describing the advisor-student relationship.

classroom_relation.name: Classroom Relation
classroom_relation.definition: A relation containing information about classrooms.

timeslot_relation.name: Timeslot Relation
timeslot_relation.definition: A relation containing information about time slots.

availability.name: Availability
availability.definition: The ability to read and write data.

replicas.name: Replicas
replicas.definition: Different copies of the same data stored across multiple servers.

scalable_database_application.name: Scalable Database Application
scalable_database_application.definition: A database application designed to handle a very large number of users.

single_server_database.name: Single Server Database System
single_server_database.definition: A database system running on a single server.

master_node.name: Master Node
master_node.definition: A node that stores the partition table.

client_nodes.name: Client Nodes
client_nodes.definition: Nodes that access data and can be used to replicate the partition table.

routers.name: Routers
routers.definition: Components that accept read/write requests from clients and forward them to the appropriate real node.

consistent_hashing.name: Consistent Hashing
consistent_hashing.definition: A hash-based partitioning scheme that ensures even distribution of keys across nodes.

key_values.name: Key Values
key_values.definition: Values used to determine which node a key should be mapped to.

node_identifiers.name: Node Identifiers
node_identifiers.definition: Identifiers of nodes that are hashed to the same space as key values.

distributed_hash_tables.name: Distributed Hash Tables
distributed_hash_tables.definition: Data structures based on consistent hashing that do not require a master node or router.

nonleaf_node.name: Nonleaf Node
nonleaf_node.definition: A component of B-tree where there are m - 1 keys and includes pointers B i.

section_entity.name: Section Entity
section_entity.definition: Uniquely identified by a course identifier, semester, year, and section identifier.

sec_course_relationship_set.name: Sec-Course Relationship Set
sec_course_relationship_set.definition: Relationship set between section and course entity sets.

horizontal_partitioning.name: Horizontal Partitioning
horizontal_partitioning.definition: Breaking up the tuples of a relation into partitions.

date_attribute.name: Date Attribute
date_attribute.definition: An attribute in a relation that stores dates.

year_month_combination.name: (Year, Month) Combination
year_month_combination.definition: A combination of year and month used for partitioning.

attribute_id.name: Attribute ID
attribute_id.definition: An attribute in a relation that is used for indexing.

projection_of_tuple.name: Projection of Tuple
projection_of_tuple.definition: A process that extracts specific attributes from a tuple.

multiset_relational_algebra_expression.name: Multiset Relational Algebra Expression
multiset_relational_algebra_expression.definition: A representation of a SQL query using relational algebra.

relational_algebra_select_operation.name: Relational Algebra Select Operation
relational_algebra_select_operation.definition: An operation that filters tuples based on a given predicate.

as_clause.name: AS Clause
as_clause.definition: A clause used to rename attributes or relations in a SQL query.

many_to_one_relationship_set_ab.name: Many-to-One Relationship Set AB
many_to_one_relationship_set_ab.definition: A relationship set from entity set A to entity set B where each entity in A participates in the relationship.

relational_schema.name: Relational Schema
relational_schema.definition: A schema constructed using a relational-schema construction algorithm.

inst_dept.name: inst_dept
inst_dept.definition: A schema combining instructor and department schemas.

stud_dept.name: stud_dept
stud_dept.definition: A schema combining student and department schemas.

course_dept.name: course_dept
course_dept.definition: A schema combining course and department schemas.

consensus.name: Consensus Algorithm
consensus.definition: An algorithm for reaching agreement on what data should be added to a blockchain.

enterprise_blockchain_environment.name: Enterprise Blockchain Environment
enterprise_blockchain_environment.definition: A blockchain environment where some organization controls who can have permission to access the blockchain.

value_vj.name: Value Vj
value_vj.definition: A value that an attribute can take.

instructor_info.name: Instructor Info
instructor_info.definition: A relation containing information about instructors.

lock_lease.name: Lock Lease
lock_lease.definition: A mechanism where a participant can acquire a lock lease for a task.

coordinator.name: Coordinator
coordinator.definition: A node responsible for managing a task.

fault_tolerant_lock_manager.name: Fault-Tolerant Lock Manager
fault_tolerant_lock_manager.definition: A lock manager that ensures only one participant can get a lock lease.

group_by_cube.name: Group By Cube
group_by_cube.definition: Generates an even larger number of groupings, consisting of all subsets of the attributes listed in the cube construct.

shadow_copy_scheme.name: Shadow Copy Scheme
shadow_copy_scheme.definition: An algorithm where a transaction creates a complete copy of the database before updating it, allowing for easy rollback if needed.

db_pointer.name: DB Pointer
db_pointer.definition: A property that identifies the current copy of the database, stored on disk.

earliest_database_systems.name: Earliest Database Systems
earliest_database_systems.definition: Database systems that arose in the 1960s in response to the computerized management of commercial data.

modern_database_applications.name: Modern Database Applications
modern_database_applications.definition: Database applications that include highly sophisticated, worldwide enterprises.

central_aspect_of_database_application.name: Central Aspect of Database Application
central_aspect_of_database_application.definition: The data themselves, not a program performing some calculation.

most_valuable_corporations.name: Most Valuable Corporations
most_valuable_corporations.definition: Corporations whose value is primarily due to the information they own.

simple_structured_data.name: Simple Structured Data
simple_structured_data.definition: Data with a standard, repeating structure, like university records.

complex_structured_data.name: Complex Structured Data
complex_structured_data.definition: Data with complex relationships and a more variable structure, like social-networking sites.

university_records.name: University Records
university_records.definition: Records regarding courses, students, and course registration at a university.

social_networking_site.name: Social-Networking Site
social_networking_site.definition: A type of modern database application with complex relationships and a more variable structure.

raid_software_implementation.name: Software RAID
raid_software_implementation.definition: A RAID implementation that uses only software modification without changing the hardware.

hardware_raid.name: Hardware RAID System
hardware_raid.definition: A RAID system that uses special-purpose hardware to support RAID.

nonvolatile_ram.name: Nonvolatile RAM
nonvolatile_ram.definition: A type of memory that retains its contents even after power loss.

pipeline_operation.name: Pipeline Operation
pipeline_operation.definition: A component in a pipeline that generates and buffers output tuples.

producer_driven_pipelining.name: Producer-Driven Pipelining
producer_driven_pipelining.definition: A method of pipelining where data is pushed up an operation tree from below.

demand_driven_pipelining.name: Demand-Driven Pipelining
demand_driven_pipelining.definition: A method of pipelining where data is pulled up an operation tree from the top.

shared_nothing_parallel_databases.name: Shared-Nothing Parallel Databases
shared_nothing_parallel_databases.definition: Parallel database systems that do not share main memory or disks.

network_latency.name: Network Latency
network_latency.definition: The time delay experienced in sending data over a network.

data_center.name: Data Center
data_center.definition: A physical location where servers and related components are housed.

n_factorial_valid_serial_schedules.name: n Factorial Valid Serial Schedules
n_factorial_valid_serial_schedules.definition: For a set of n transactions, there exist n factorial (n!) different valid serial schedules.

concurrent_transactions.name: Concurrent Transactions
concurrent_transactions.definition: Transactions running concurrently where the operating system may execute one transaction for a while, then switch to another transaction.

context_switch.name: Context Switch
context_switch.definition: The process by which the operating system switches from executing one transaction to another.

cpu_time_sharing.name: CPU Time Sharing
cpu_time_sharing.definition: The CPU time is shared among all the transactions when they are executed concurrently.

transaction_schedule.name: Transaction Schedule
transaction_schedule.definition: The sequence in which transactions are executed, whether serially or concurrently.

figure_17_4_schedule.name: Figure 17.4 Schedule
figure_17_4_schedule.definition: A specific schedule for two concurrent transactions as illustrated in Figure 17.4.

figure_17_5_schedule.name: Figure 17.5 Schedule
figure_17_5_schedule.definition: Another specific schedule for two concurrent transactions as illustrated in Figure 17.5.

unique_role_assumption.name: Unique Role Assumption
unique_role_assumption.definition: Each attribute name has a unique meaning in the database.

instructor_schema.name: Instructor Schema
instructor_schema.definition: A schema for the instructor entity set.

classroom_schema.name: Classroom Schema
classroom_schema.definition: A schema for the classroom entity set.

person_entity_set.name: Person Entity Set
person_entity_set.definition: A generalized entity set combining instructor and student entity sets.

student_entity_set.name: Student Entity Set
student_entity_set.definition: A specific entity set for students.

tree_protocol.name: Tree Protocol
tree_protocol.definition: A protocol where a data item that has been locked and unlocked by T i cannot subsequently be relocked by T i.

conflict_serializable.name: Conflict Serializable
conflict_serializable.definition: All schedules that are legal under the tree protocol are conflict serializable.

database_graph.name: Database Graph
database_graph.definition: A graph used to illustrate the tree protocol.

transaction_t10.name: Transaction T10
transaction_t10.definition: A transaction that follows the tree protocol with specific lock and unlock instructions.

transaction_t11.name: Transaction T11
transaction_t11.definition: A transaction that follows the tree protocol with specific lock and unlock instructions.

transaction_t12.name: Transaction T12
transaction_t12.definition: A transaction that follows the tree protocol with specific lock and unlock instructions.

transaction_t13.name: Transaction T13
transaction_t13.definition: A transaction that follows the tree protocol with specific lock and unlock instructions.

schedule.name: Schedule
schedule.definition: A possible sequence of operations performed by transactions.

figure_18_11.name: Figure 18.11
figure_18_11.definition: A figure showing a tree-structured database graph.

figure_18_12.name: Figure 18.12
figure_18_12.definition: A figure showing a possible schedule in which the four transactions participated.

tape.name: Tape
tape.definition: A type of physical storage media with high capacity and removable tapes.

tape_drive.name: Tape Drive
tape_drive.definition: A device that reads and writes data to and from tapes.

tape_library.name: Tape Library
tape_library.definition: A collection of tapes stored in a jukebox-like device for automated storage and retrieval.

storage_hierarchy.name: Storage Hierarchy
storage_hierarchy.definition: A concept where storage devices are organized based on their speed and cost.

primary_storage.name: Primary Storage
primary_storage.definition: The fastest storage media in the hierarchy, such as cache and main memory.

wait_for_graph.name: Wait-for Graph
wait_for_graph.definition: A visual representation showing a cycle which indicates a deadlock.

deadlock_detection.name: Deadlock Detection Algorithm
deadlock_detection.definition: An algorithm used to detect deadlocks in a system.

allocation_request.name: Allocation Request
allocation_request.definition: A request for resource allocation that cannot be granted immediately.

double_pipelined_join.name: Double-Pipelined Join Algorithm
double_pipelined_join.definition: A join algorithm that is pipelined on both its inputs and its output.

double_pipelined_hash_join.name: Double-Pipelined Hash-Join Technique
double_pipelined_hash_join.definition: A join technique using hash indices on relations r and s.

end_r_entry.name: End r Entry
end_r_entry.definition: A special queue entry serving as an end-of-file marker for relation r.

end_s_entry.name: End s Entry
end_s_entry.definition: A special queue entry serving as an end-of-file marker for relation s.

queue.name: Queue
queue.definition: A single queue where tuples from both input relations are queued for processing.

race_condition.name: Race Condition
race_condition.definition: A situation where two or more concurrent operations can cause incorrect results if they are not properly synchronized.

security_constraint.name: Security Constraint
security_constraint.definition: A rule that restricts access to certain parts of the database based on user roles and responsibilities.

join_size_estimation.name: Join Size Estimation
join_size_estimation.definition: The process of estimating the size of a join operation based on the values of attributes in the relations being joined.

v_a_r.name: V(A, r)
v_a_r.definition: The set of values for attribute A in relation r.

dangling_tuples.name: Dangling Tuples
dangling_tuples.definition: Tuples that do not match any tuple in the other relation during a join operation.

backup_coordinator_node.name: Backup Coordinator Node
backup_coordinator_node.definition: A node that maintains enough information locally to allow it to assume the role of coordinator with minimal disruption to the distributed system.

actual_coordinator.name: Actual Coordinator
actual_coordinator.definition: The node currently executing the coordination tasks in the distributed system.

data_isolation.name: Data Isolation
data_isolation.definition: Because data are scattered in various files, and files may be in different formats, writing new application programs to retrieve the appropriate data is difficult.

integrity_problems.name: Integrity Problems
integrity_problems.definition: The data values stored in the database must satisfy certain types of consistency constraints.

atomicity_problems.name: Atomicity Problems
atomicity_problems.definition: A computer system, like any other device, is subject to failure. In many applications, it is crucial that, if a failure occurs, the data be restored to the consistent state that existed prior to the failure.

file_systems_and_database_storage_struct.name: File Systems and Database Storage Structures
file_systems_and_database_storage_struct.definition: Components that can see an identical logical view of the underlying storage structure, regardless of whether it is flash or magnetic storage.

ssd_performance.name: SSD Performance
ssd_performance.definition: Performance metrics of solid-state drives, including random block reads, data transfer rates for sequential reads and writes, and random block writes.

random_block_reads_per_second.name: Random Block Reads Per Second
random_block_reads_per_second.definition: A measure of how many random 4-kilobyte blocks can be read per second by an SSD.

sequential_reads_and_writes.name: Sequential Reads and Writes
sequential_reads_and_writes.definition: Data transfer rates for reading and writing data sequentially on an SSD.

flash_disk.name: Flash Disk
flash_disk.definition: A type of SSD with SATA interface that can support nearly 100,000 random 4-kilobyte block reads in a second with 32 requests sent in parallel.

nvme_pcie.name: NVMe PCIe
nvme_pcie.definition: An interface that allows SSDs to support over 350,000 random 4-kilobyte block reads per second.

region_query.name: Region Query
region_query.definition: A query that deals with spatial regions and can ask for objects that lie partially or fully inside a specified region.

retail_shop.name: Retail Shop
retail_shop.definition: An example of an object that can be queried using a region query.

postgis_st_contains.name: ST_Contains()
postgis_st_contains.definition: A function supported by PostGIS that checks if one geometry or geography object contains another.

nearness_query.name: Nearness Query
nearness_query.definition: A query that requests objects that lie near a specified location.

restaurant.name: Restaurant
restaurant.definition: An example of an object that can be queried using a nearness query.

nearest_neighbor_query.name: Nearest Neighbor Query
nearest_neighbor_query.definition: A query that requests the object that is nearest to a specified point.

gasoline_station.name: Gasoline Station
gasoline_station.definition: An example of an object that can be queried using a nearest neighbor query.

free_space_map.name: Free Space Map
free_space_map.definition: A component that tracks free space in blocks.

optical_storage_medium.name: Optical Storage Medium
optical_storage_medium.definition: A type of storage medium that uses laser light to write and read data.

digital_video_disk.name: Digital Video Disk (DVD)
digital_video_disk.definition: An optical storage medium used to store video data and other types of digital data.

blu_ray_dvd_format.name: Blu-ray DVD Format
blu_ray_dvd_format.definition: A specific type of DVD format with a capacity ranging from 27 gigabytes to 128 gigabytes.

write_once_read_many_disks.name: Write Once, Read Many (WORM) Disks
write_once_read_many_disks.definition: Disks that can be written once but cannot be overwritten.

optical_disk_jukebox.name: Optical Disk Jukebox System
optical_disk_jukebox.definition: A system containing a few drives and numerous disks that can be loaded automatically.

multivalued_dependency_id.name: Multivalued Dependency
multivalued_dependency_id.definition: A type of dependency where a single value in one attribute can correspond to multiple values in another attribute.

functional_dependency_id.name: Functional Dependency
functional_dependency_id.definition: A type of dependency where a single value in one attribute determines a single value in another attribute.

relation_id.name: Relation
relation_id.definition: A set of tuples that represent a specific table in a database.

figure_7_15_id.name: Figure 7.15
figure_7_15_id.definition: A figure showing an illegal relation in the context of multivalued dependencies.

iterator_expression.name: Iterator Expression
iterator_expression.definition: Applies the split function to create an array of words, converts the array to a list with Arrays.asList, and creates an iterator from the list.

words_rdd.name: Words RDD
words_rdd.definition: An RDD containing each record as a single word.

ones_java_pair_rdd.name: Ones JavaPairRDD
ones_java_pair_rdd.definition: A JavaPairRDD containing pairs of the form (word, 1) for each word in words.

reduce_by_key_function.name: ReduceByKey Function
reduce_by_key_function.definition: A function that groups by the first attribute and aggregates the values of the second attribute using the provided lambda function.

addition_lambda_function.name: Addition Lambda Function
addition_lambda_function.definition: A lambda function (i1, i2) -> i1 + i2 passed to reduceByKey() to perform addition.

authorization_mechanism.name: Authorization Mechanism
authorization_mechanism.definition: A mechanism to control access to data and functionality within an enterprise application.

database_authorization_features.name: Database Authorization Features
database_authorization_features.definition: Features used to implement authorization at the database level.

aggregate_function.name: Aggregate Function
aggregate_function.definition: Functions that take a collection of values as input and return a single value.

avg.name: Average
avg.definition: A standard built-in aggregate function in SQL that calculates the average of a collection of numbers.

min.name: Minimum
min.definition: A standard built-in aggregate function in SQL that finds the smallest value in a collection.

max.name: Maximum
max.definition: A standard built-in aggregate function in SQL that finds the largest value in a collection.

sum.name: Total
sum.definition: A standard built-in aggregate function in SQL that adds up all the values in a collection of numbers.

count.name: Count
count.definition: A standard built-in aggregate function in SQL that counts the number of elements in a collection.

atomic_execution.name: Atomic Execution
atomic_execution.definition: Transaction execution is said to be atomic if despite failures, either all the data items updated by the transaction are successfully updated, or all the data items are reverted back to their original values.

sequential_file.name: Sequential File
sequential_file.definition: A file designed for efficient processing of records in sorted order based on some search key.

pointer_chain.name: Pointer Chain
pointer_chain.definition: A method of chaining records together by pointers to allow fast retrieval of records in search-key order.

instructor_records.name: Instructor Records
instructor_records.definition: Records of instructors stored in a sequential file with ID as the search key.

four_normal_form_decomposition.name: 4NF Decomposition Algorithm
four_normal_form_decomposition.definition: An algorithm for decomposing a schema into 4NF, similar to BCNF but using multivalued dependencies.

three_normal_form.name: 3NF Algorithm
three_normal_form.definition: An algorithm that ensures the preservation of dependencies by explicitly building a schema for each dependency in a canonical cover.

canonical_cover.name: Canonical Cover
canonical_cover.definition: A set of dependencies where every attribute on the left-hand side is minimal.

three_normal_form_design.name: 3NF Design
three_normal_form_design.definition: A database design that satisfies the third normal form, ensuring that all non-key attributes are fully functionally dependent on the primary key.

functional_dependency_alpha_beta.name: Functional Dependency α → β
functional_dependency_alpha_beta.definition: A functional dependency in the form α → β, where α ⊆ R and β ⊆ R.

bcnf_database_design.name: BCNF Database Design
bcnf_database_design.definition: A database design is in BCNF if each member of the set of relation schemas that constitutes the design is in BCNF.

java_persistence_api_jpa.name: Java Persistence API (JPA)
java_persistence_api_jpa.definition: An API implemented by Hibernate for managing persistence in Java applications.

mapping_file.name: Mapping File
mapping_file.definition: A file specifying the mapping from each Java class to one or more relations.

properties_file.name: Properties File
properties_file.definition: A file containing information about the database, such as the host and credentials.

session.name: Session
session.definition: A component that sets up the connection to the database.

student_class.name: Student Class
student_class.definition: A Java class representing a student.

takes_relationship.name: Takes Relationship
takes_relationship.definition: A relationship between student and section in an E-R model.

unlock_message.name: Unlock Message
unlock_message.definition: A message sent to the lock manager indicating that a transaction is releasing a lock on a data item.

distributed_validation.name: Distributed Validation
distributed_validation.definition: A process used to ensure consistency in distributed databases.

startts.name: StartTS
startts.definition: A property representing the start timestamp of a transaction.

finishts.name: FinishTS
finishts.definition: A property representing the finish timestamp of a transaction.

transaction_t_37.name: Transaction T 37
transaction_t_37.definition: A transaction that withdraws $200 from a savings account.

serial_execution.name: Serial Execution
serial_execution.definition: An order in which transactions are executed sequentially without interference.

bill_number_sequence.name: Bill Number Sequence
bill_number_sequence.definition: A sequence used to generate unique bill numbers by taking the maximum current bill number and adding 1.

shuffle_step.name: Shuffle Step
shuffle_step.definition: A process that performs data exchange between machines and then sorts (key, value) pairs to bring all the values for a key together.

reduce_function.name: Reduce Function
reduce_function.definition: A function that processes the intermediate (key, value) pairs produced by the map function.

word_count_example.name: Word Count Example
word_count_example.definition: An example where the outputs of the map() functions are reorganized to bring all the values for a particular key together.

special_purpose_data_structures.name: Special-Purpose Data Structures
special_purpose_data_structures.definition: Data structures used by some database systems to store metadata.

database_relations.name: Database Relations
database_relations.definition: Relations in the database used to store system metadata.

index_metadata.name: Index Metadata
index_metadata.definition: A relation storing information about indexes, possibly in a non-normalized form.

3nf.name: 3NF
3nf.definition: A normal form for relational database schemas that ensures losslessness and dependency preservation but may require null values and repetition of information.

multiple_top_of_rack_switches.name: Multiple Top-of-Rack Switches
multiple_top_of_rack_switches.definition: Also referred to as edge switches, these can be connected to another switch called an aggregation switch.

aggregation_switch.name: Aggregation Switch
aggregation_switch.definition: A switch that connects a group of racks in a tree topology with three tiers.

core_switch.name: Core Switch
core_switch.definition: The topmost switch in the tree topology that also provides connectivity to outside networks.

tree_topology.name: Tree Topology
tree_topology.definition: A network architecture with three tiers, including a core switch at the top, aggregation switches in the middle, and top-of-rack switches at the bottom.

interconnects.name: Interconnects
interconnects.definition: The connections between switches that provide bandwidth for communication between racks.

monetary_cost.name: Monetary Cost
monetary_cost.definition: The cost of extra disk-storage requirements.

io_operations_per_second.name: I/O Operations Per Second
io_operations_per_second.definition: Performance requirement measured in the number of input/output operations per second.

performance_when_disk_fails.name: Performance When Disk Fails
performance_when_disk_fails.definition: Performance of the system when a disk has failed.

rebuild_performance.name: Rebuild Performance
rebuild_performance.definition: Performance during the process of rebuilding data on a new disk after a disk failure.

raid_level_1.name: RAID Level 1
raid_level_1.definition: A RAID level where data can be copied from another disk for easy rebuild.

raid_level_0.name: RAID Level 0
raid_level_0.definition: A RAID level used in high-performance applications where data safety is not critical.

multivalued_data_type.name: Multivalued Data Type
multivalued_data_type.definition: A type of data structure used in scientific experiments and industrial monitoring applications where readings from multiple sensors are stored.

non_first_normal_form_data.name: Non First-Normal-Form (NFNF) Data Model
non_first_normal_form_data.definition: A data model that supports multivalued attribute types, proposed early in the history of databases.

array_database.name: Array Database
array_database.definition: A database that provides specialized support for arrays, including efficient compressed storage and query language extensions.

oracle_georaster.name: Oracle GeoRaster
oracle_georaster.definition: An example of an array database extension for Oracle.

postgis_extension.name: PostGIS Extension
postgis_extension.definition: An example of an array database extension for PostgreSQL.

sciql_extension.name: SciQL Extension
sciql_extension.definition: An example of an array database extension for MonetDB.

scidb_database.name: SciDB Database
scidb_database.definition: A database tailored for scientific applications with features for array data types.

database_user.name: Database User
database_user.definition: A person who works with a database but does not manage it.

database_administrator.name: Database Administrator
database_administrator.definition: A person who manages a database.

storage_area_network.name: Storage Area Network
storage_area_network.definition: A network that connects multiple computers to shared storage devices.

shared_memory.name: Shared Memory System
shared_memory.definition: A type of parallel system where multiple processors have direct access to a shared memory space.

communication_network.name: Communication Network
communication_network.definition: A network used for communication between different nodes in a distributed system.

io_parallelism.name: I/O Parallelism
io_parallelism.definition: A technique where the transfer rates for reading or writing an entire relation are much faster.

round_robin_partitioning.name: Round-Robin Partitioning
round_robin_partitioning.definition: A scheme ideally suited for applications that wish to read the entire relation sequentially for each query.

hash_partitioning.name: Hash Partitioning
hash_partitioning.definition: A scheme best suited for point queries based on the partitioning attribute.

point_queries.name: Point Queries
point_queries.definition: Queries seeking tuples that have a specified value for a specific attribute.

range_queries.name: Range Queries
range_queries.definition: Queries locating all tuples for which the value of a given attribute lies within a specified range.

pipelined_edges.name: Pipelined Edges
pipelined_edges.definition: Edges where the output of the producer is sent directly to the consumer without being written to disk.

materialized_edges.name: Materialized Edges
materialized_edges.definition: Edges where the output is written to disk and then read from the disk by the consumer.

evaluation_plan.name: Evaluation Plan
evaluation_plan.definition: A plan that computes the same result as the given relational-algebra expression in the most efficient way.

sort_operator.name: Sort Operator
sort_operator.definition: An operator that can be represented using suboperators with materialized edges between the suboperators.

hash_join_operator.name: Hash Join Operator
hash_join_operator.definition: An operator that can be represented using suboperators with materialized edges between the suboperators.

instructor_tuples.name: Instructor Tuples
instructor_tuples.definition: Tuples representing instructors in the database.

logical_error.name: Logical Error
logical_error.definition: An error within a transaction that causes it to stop executing due to conditions like bad input, data not found, overflow, or resource limits.

system_error.name: System Error
system_error.definition: An error in the system that prevents a transaction from continuing, but allows the transaction to be re-executed later.

failstop_assumption.name: Failstop Assumption
failstop_assumption.definition: The assumption that hardware errors and software bugs will halt the system without corrupting non-volatile storage contents.

relational_operations.name: Relational Operations
relational_operations.definition: Operations that can be expressed by a sequence of Map and reduce steps.

outerjoin.name: Outer Join
outerjoin.definition: A variant of the join operation.

alpha_closure.name: α +
alpha_closure.definition: The closure of attribute set α

beta_closure.name: β
beta_closure.definition: The closure of attribute set β

gamma_closure.name: γ +
gamma_closure.definition: The closure of attribute set γ

r_closure.name: R +
r_closure.definition: The closure of attribute set R

student_registration_query.name: Student Registration Query
student_registration_query.definition: A query that retrieves registration information for a specific student ID.

materialized_view.name: Materialized View
materialized_view.definition: A precomputed result stored in a database that can be used to speed up queries.

document_stores.name: Document Stores
document_stores.definition: A type of key-value storage system that allows the stored data to follow a specified data representation, enabling the data store to interpret the stored values and execute simple queries based on stored values.

mongodb.name: MongoDB
mongodb.definition: A widely used data store that accepts values in the JSON format.

put_function.name: put(key, value)
put_function.definition: A function used to store values with an associated key in a key-value storage system.
