spatial_join.definition: A process that generates pairs of objects that intersect or the intersection regions of such pairs given two relations with spatial objects.

spatial_relations.name: Spatial Relations
spatial_relations.definition: Relations containing spatial objects used in spatial joins.

spatial_predicates.name: Spatial Predicates
spatial_predicates.definition: Predicates like ST_Contains() or ST_Overlaps() used as join predicates in spatial joins.

rename_operator.name: Rename Operator
rename_operator.definition: An operator denoted by the lowercase Greek letter rho (ρ) that allows giving names to the results of relational-algebra expressions.

relational_algebra_expression.name: Relational-Algebra Expression
relational_algebra_expression.definition: A mathematical expression in relational algebra that represents a set of operations on relations.

exclusive_locks.name: Exclusive Locks
exclusive_locks.definition: A type of lock that prevents any other transaction from accessing the locked data item.

transaction_commit.name: Transaction Commit
transaction_commit.definition: The process of finalizing a transaction and making its changes permanent.

remote_data_center.name: Remote Data Center
remote_data_center.definition: A data center located at a distance from the primary data center.

network_round_trip_time.name: Network Round-Trip Time
network_round_trip_time.definition: The total time taken for a message to travel from one point to another and back again over a network.

data_item_lock_duration.name: Data Item Lock Duration
data_item_lock_duration.definition: The length of time a lock is held on a data item during a transaction.

user_data_in_web_application.name: User Data in Web Application
user_data_in_web_application.definition: Data related to users in a web application.

input_relations_r_and_s.name: Input Relations R and S
input_relations_r_and_s.definition: The relations being joined in the merge-join operation.

disconnected_operation.name: Disconnected Operation
disconnected_operation.definition: Supporting some operations even when a client is disconnected from the application server.

local_storage.name: Local Storage
local_storage.definition: A feature of the HTML5 standard that allows storing data locally on the client machine.

storage_check_code.name: Storage Check Code
storage_check_code.definition: A JavaScript code snippet to check if the browser supports local storage.

set_item_function.name: setItem Function
set_item_function.definition: A function to store a value for a given key in local storage.

get_item_function.name: getItem Function
get_item_function.definition: A function to retrieve a value for a given key from local storage.

delete_item_function.name: deleteItem Function
delete_item_function.definition: A function to delete a value for a given key from local storage.

maximum_data_storage_limit.name: Maximum Data Storage Limit
maximum_data_storage_limit.definition: The maximum amount of data a web site can store locally on the client machine, typically 5 megabytes.

commit_timestamp.name: Commit Timestamp
commit_timestamp.definition: A timestamp indicating when a transaction commits.

file_mapping.name: File Mapping
file_mapping.definition: Mapping the database to files using several files with records of only one fixed length.

fixed_length_records_file.name: Fixed-Length Records File
fixed_length_records_file.definition: A file where all records have the same fixed length.

variable_length_records_file.name: Variable-Length Records File
variable_length_records_file.definition: A file where records can have different lengths.

hibernate_orm.name: Hibernate ORM
hibernate_orm.definition: A system that translates HQL queries to SQL and converts results into objects.

student_objects.name: Student Objects
student_objects.definition: Objects representing students, created from database results.

django_orm.name: Django ORM
django_orm.definition: An ORM component of the Django framework used for defining models in Python.

advisor_relationship.name: Advisor Relationship
advisor_relationship.definition: A many-to-many relationship between Student and Instructor.

l_0.name: L0
l_0.definition: The first level of the LSM tree, which is in memory.

l_i.name: Li
l_i.definition: The ith level of the LSM tree, where i > 0.

l_i_plus_1.name: Li+1
l_i_plus_1.definition: The (i+1)th level of the LSM tree, where i >= 0.

m.name: m
m.definition: The number of entries in a leaf of Li.

k.name: k
k.definition: A factor used to determine the maximum size of each Li+1 relative to Li.

m_over_k.name: m/k
m_over_k.definition: The number of entries in a leaf of Li+1.

size_of_l_i.name: Size of Li
size_of_l_i.definition: The size of the tree at level Li, given by k^i * M.

total_number_of_levels_r.name: r
total_number_of_levels_r.definition: The total number of levels in the LSM tree, approximately log_k(I/M).

i_o_operations_per_insert.name: (k/m)log_k(I/M)
i_o_operations_per_insert.definition: The total number of I/O operations required for each insert in an LSM tree.

system_metadata.name: System Metadata
system_metadata.definition: Frequently accessed information stored in the database.

in_memory_data_structures.name: In-Memory Data Structures
in_memory_data_structures.definition: Data structures stored in memory for efficient access.

sigma_a_equal_a_r.name: σ A = a ( r )
sigma_a_equal_a_r.definition: A selection operation that filters records based on a specific value in a given attribute.

uniform_distribution.name: Uniform Distribution
uniform_distribution.definition: An assumption where each value appears with equal probability.

course_id_attribute.name: course_id attribute
course_id_attribute.definition: An attribute in the takes relation used to identify courses.

binary_tree_partition.name: Binary Tree Partition
binary_tree_partition.definition: Each internal node of a binary tree partitions a one-dimensional interval in two.

balanced_binary_tree_partition.name: Balanced Binary Tree Partition
balanced_binary_tree_partition.definition: In a balanced binary tree, the partition is chosen so that approximately one-half of the points stored in the subtree fall in each partition.

b_plus_tree_partition.name: B+ Tree Partition
b_plus_tree_partition.definition: Each level of a B+ -tree splits a one-dimensional interval into multiple parts.

k_d_tree_partition.name: k-d Tree Partition
k_d_tree_partition.definition: Each level of a k-d tree partitions the space into two, cycling through dimensions.

basic_lsm_tree.name: Basic LSM Tree
basic_lsm_tree.definition: A data structure used in lookup operations where the number of tree accesses is reduced.

special_concurrency_control_techniques.name: Special-purpose Concurrency Control Techniques
special_concurrency_control_techniques.definition: Concurrency control techniques specifically designed for index structures.

latch_free_data_structures.name: Latch-free Data Structures
latch_free_data_structures.definition: Data structures designed to reduce concurrency control overheads in main-memory databases.

increment_of_a_counter.name: Increment of a Counter
increment_of_a_counter.definition: An operation considered as a basic unit for concurrency control.

multitable_clustering_file_organization.name: Multitable Clustering File Organization
multitable_clustering_file_organization.definition: A file organization that stores related records of two or more relations in each block.

pointer.name: Pointer
pointer.definition: A reference to another node within the B+ tree.

fanout.name: Fanout
fanout.definition: The number of pointers in a node in a B+ tree.

checkpointing.name: Checkpointing Technique
checkpointing.definition: A method for periodically saving the state of a database to ensure recovery in case of failure.

last_checkpoint.name: Last Checkpoint
last_checkpoint.definition: The location in the log of the checkpoint record of the last completed checkpoint stored in a fixed position on disk.

modified_buffer_blocks.name: Modified Buffer Blocks
modified_buffer_blocks.definition: A list of all buffer blocks that have been modified and need to be written to disk.

deadlock_detection_and_recovery.name: Deadlock Detection and Recovery
deadlock_detection_and_recovery.definition: A process that involves detecting and recovering from deadlocks in a system.

periodic_state_examination.name: Periodic State Examination Algorithm
periodic_state_examination.definition: An algorithm that examines the state of the system periodically to determine if a deadlock has occurred.

deadlock_state.name: Deadlock State
deadlock_state.definition: A state where the system has entered a deadlock condition.

realworld_optimizers.name: Realworld Optimizers
realworld_optimizers.definition: Realworld optimizers often maintain further statistical information to improve the accuracy of their cost estimates of evaluation plans.

equiwidth_histogram.name: Equiwidth Histogram
equiwidth_histogram.definition: An equiwidth histogram divides the range of values into equal-sized ranges.

equidepth_histogram.name: Equidepth Histogram
equidepth_histogram.definition: An equidepth histogram adjusts the boundaries of the ranges such that each range has the same number of values.

person_tuples.name: Person Tuples
person_tuples.definition: With each range we store a count of the number of person tuples whose age values lie in that range.

sql_data_definition_language.name: SQL Data-Definition Language
sql_data_definition_language.definition: A rich DDL that allows one to define tables with data types and integrity constraints.

primary_key_integrity_constraint.name: Primary Key Integrity Constraint
primary_key_integrity_constraint.definition: Ensures that no two departments can have the same department name.

foreign_key_integrity_constraint.name: Foreign Key Integrity Constraint
foreign_key_integrity_constraint.definition: Ensures that the dept_name attribute value in any instructor record must also appear in the dept_name attribute of some record of the department table.

weak_entity_set_a.name: Weak Entity Set A
weak_entity_set_a.definition: A weak entity set with attributes a1, a2,..., am.

strong_entity_set_b.name: Strong Entity Set B
strong_entity_set_b.definition: A strong entity set on which A depends, with primary key consisting of attributes b1, b2,..., bn.

javascript.name: JavaScript
javascript.definition: A programming language used to create highly responsive user interfaces within a browser.

document_object_model_dom.name: Document Object Model (DOM)
document_object_model_dom.definition: A standard for parsing HTML code into an in-memory tree structure.

jquery_library.name: JQuery Library
jquery_library.definition: A JavaScript library that allows code to be written in a browser-independent way.

database_instance.name: Database Instance
database_instance.definition: The collection of information stored in the database at a particular moment.

database_schema.name: Database Schema
database_schema.definition: The overall design of the database.

variable_declaration.name: Variable Declaration
variable_declaration.definition: The part of a program that defines the type of a variable.

physical_schema.name: Physical Schema
physical_schema.definition: Describes the database design at the physical level.

logical_schema.name: Logical Schema
logical_schema.definition: Describes the database design at the logical level.

view_level_schema.name: View Level Schema
view_level_schema.definition: Describes different views of the database.

write_request.name: Write Request
write_request.definition: A request to write data to a specific tablet.

insert_request.name: Insert Request
insert_request.definition: A request to add new data to a specific tablet.

growing_phase.name: Growing Phase
growing_phase.definition: A phase during which a transaction may obtain locks but not release any lock.

shrinking_phase.name: Shrinking Phase
shrinking_phase.definition: A phase during which a transaction may release locks but not obtain any new locks.

lock_point.name: Lock Point
lock_point.definition: The point in the schedule where a transaction has obtained its final lock (end of its growing phase).

entity.name: Entity
entity.definition: Any distinctly identifiable item such as people, places, products, instructors, students, departments, courses, and course offerings.

course_offering.name: Course Offering
course_offering.definition: A specific instance of a course being offered, possibly in multiple semesters and times within a semester.

redundancy.name: Redundancy
redundancy.definition: A situation where the same information is stored multiple times, unnecessarily.

get_connection.name: getConnection() Method
get_connection.definition: A method of the DriverManager class within java.sql that opens a connection to a database.

driver_manager_class.name: DriverManager Class
driver_manager_class.definition: A class within java.sql that contains the getConnection() method for opening a connection to a database.

url_string.name: URL String
url_string.definition: A string that specifies the URL, or machine name, where the server runs, along with possibly some other information such as the protocol, port number, and specific database.

database_user_identifier.name: Database User Identifier
database_user_identifier.definition: A database user identifier, which is a second parameter to the getConnection() method.

in_memory_sorting.name: In-Memory Sorting Algorithm
in_memory_sorting.definition: An algorithm used to sort data that fits within the cache.

cache_conscious.name: Cache-Conscious Algorithm
cache_conscious.definition: An algorithm designed to minimize cache misses.

build_relation.name: Build Relation
build_relation.definition: The relation used to build the index in a hash join operation.

probe_phase.name: Probe Phase
probe_phase.definition: The phase in a hash join where the index is used to find matching rows.

partition.name: Partition
partition.definition: A division of a relation into smaller pieces for processing.

waiting_transactions_set.name: Set of Waiting Transactions
waiting_transactions_set.definition: A set of waiting transactions { T 0, T 1,..., T n } such that each transaction is waiting for a data item held by another transaction in the set.

transaction_rollback.name: Transaction Rollback
transaction_rollback.definition: Rolling back some of the transactions involved in the deadlock to resolve the situation.

deadlock_prevention_protocol.name: Deadlock Prevention Protocol
deadlock_prevention_protocol.definition: A method to ensure that the system will never enter a deadlock state.

deadlock_detection_and_recovery_scheme.name: Deadlock Detection and Recovery Scheme
deadlock_detection_and_recovery_scheme.definition: A method to detect and recover from a deadlock state.

bank_database_accounts.name: Bank Database with Accounts A and B
bank_database_accounts.definition: A database consisting of two accounts A and B with the consistency requirement that the sum A + B be preserved.

non_conflict_serializable_schedule.name: Non-Conflict-Serializable Schedule
non_conflict_serializable_schedule.definition: A schedule of transactions that is not conflict serializable but still preserves the sum of A + B.

timestamp_and_validation_protocol.name: Timestamp and Validation Protocol
timestamp_and_validation_protocol.definition: A protocol that has similar problems to two-phase locking in terms of concurrency when many transactions conflict on a particular data item.

sales_transaction.name: Sales Transaction
sales_transaction.definition: A transaction that updates the materialized view daily_sales_total as part of the transaction.

daily_sales_total.name: Daily Sales Total
daily_sales_total.definition: A materialized view that records total sales on each day.

dynamic_sql.name: Dynamic SQL
dynamic_sql.definition: Most current systems use dynamic SQL, rather than embedded SQL.

microsoft_language_integrated_query_linq.name: Microsoft Language Integrated Query (LINQ)
microsoft_language_integrated_query_linq.definition: A facility that extends the host language to include support for queries.

cyclic_waits.name: Cyclic Waits
cyclic_waits.definition: No cyclic waits can occur by ordering the requests for locks, or requiring all locks to be acquired together.

simplest_scheme.name: Simplest Scheme
simplest_scheme.definition: Each transaction locks all its data items before it begins execution, and either all are locked in one step or none are locked.

transaction_protocol.name: Transaction Protocol
transaction_protocol.definition: A protocol that requires each transaction to lock all its data items before it begins execution.

total_order_protocol.name: Total Order Protocol
total_order_protocol.definition: A protocol that uses a total order of data items, in conjunction with two-phase locking.

controller.name: Disk Controller
controller.definition: A component that manages communication between the computer and the magnetic disk.

read_failure.name: Read Failure
read_failure.definition: An error condition where the disk controller fails to successfully read data from a sector.

bad_sector.name: Bad Sector
bad_sector.definition: A damaged sector on the disk that cannot be used for reading or writing data.

remapping.name: Remapping
remapping.definition: The process of mapping a bad sector to a different physical location on the disk.

algebraic_operators.name: Algebraic Operators
algebraic_operators.definition: Algebraic operators that can work on datasets containing records with complex data types, and returning datasets with records containing similar complex data types.

check_clause.name: Check Clause
check_clause.definition: A component in SQL that includes a predicate.

versionvector_scheme.name: Version Vector Scheme
versionvector_scheme.definition: A scheme for detecting inconsistent updates.

time_varying_address.name: Time-Varying Address
time_varying_address.definition: An address that changes over time.

valid_time.name: Valid Time
valid_time.definition: The time interval during which an entity or its attributes are valid.

tree_like_architecture.name: Tree-Like Architecture
tree_like_architecture.definition: A network design where each top-of-rack switch can route its messages through any of the aggregation switches it is connected to, and each aggregation switch can communicate with another aggregation switch via any of the core switches it is connected to.

top_of_rack_switch.name: Top-of-Rack Switch
top_of_rack_switch.definition: A switch in a network that is located at the top of each rack.

data_center_fabric.name: Data Center Fabric
data_center_fabric.definition: The complex interconnection networks in a data center.

indices.name: Indices
indices.definition: Indices are forms of data derived from underlying data.

publish_subscribe_systems.name: Publish-Subscribe Systems
publish_subscribe_systems.definition: Publish-subscribe systems are used to deliver information about updates to the underlying data.

real_world_index_selection_tools.name: Real-world Index Selection Tools
real_world_index_selection_tools.definition: Tools used for real-world index and materialized-view selection.

greedy_selection.name: Greedy Selection
greedy_selection.definition: A technique used by real-world index and materialized-view selection tools.

parallel_database_partitioning.name: Parallel Database Partitioning
parallel_database_partitioning.definition: An aspect of physical database design involving deciding how to partition a relation in a parallel database.

physical_storage_mechanism.name: Physical Storage Mechanism
physical_storage_mechanism.definition: A physical storage mechanism for a relation in a database.

modern_enterprise.name: Modern Enterprise
modern_enterprise.definition: An enterprise that needs to balance the efficiencies of structured data with situations where a predetermined structure is limiting.

atomicity_of_transactions.name: Atomicity of Transactions
atomicity_of_transactions.definition: Ensures that all operations of a transaction are completed successfully or none are.

composite_search_key.name: Composite Search Key
composite_search_key.definition: A combination of two attributes, a search key and a primary key, used to ensure uniqueness in an index.

binary_search.name: Binary Search
binary_search.definition: A search algorithm that works by repeatedly dividing in half the portion of the list that could contain the item.

sequential_search.name: Sequential Search
sequential_search.definition: An algorithm that sequentially scans through all elements of a list until it finds the desired element.

sparse_outer_index.name: Sparse Outer Index
sparse_outer_index.definition: A component of a two-level index structure that is used to locate records in the inner index.

two_level_sparse_index.name: Two-Level Sparse Index
two_level_sparse_index.definition: A type of index structure consisting of an outer index and an inner index.

commutativity_rule.name: Commutativity Rule
commutativity_rule.definition: The order of attributes differs between the left-hand side and right-hand side of the commutativity rule, so the equivalence does not hold if the order of attributes is taken into account.

theta_joins.name: Theta Joins
theta_joins.definition: Theta joins are associative in the following manner: where θ 2 involves attributes from only E 2 and E 3.

text_mining.name: Text Mining
text_mining.definition: Applying data-mining techniques to textual documents.

sentiment_analysis.name: Sentiment Analysis
sentiment_analysis.definition: A text mining task that analyzes the sentiment of reviews; specific words correlate with positive or negative sentiments.

information_extraction.name: Information Extraction
information_extraction.definition: A text mining task that creates structured information from unstructured textual descriptions or semi-structured data.

entity_recognition.name: Entity Recognition
entity_recognition.definition: Identifying mentions of entities in text and disambiguating them.

schema_diagram.name: Schema Diagram
schema_diagram.definition: A visual representation of a database schema, showing relations and their attributes.

two_headed_arrow.name: Two-Headed Arrow
two_headed_arrow.definition: A symbol used in schema diagrams to represent a referential integrity constraint that is not a foreign-key constraint.

blockchain_fork.name: Blockchain Fork
blockchain_fork.definition: A situation where two nodes add a new block at nearly the same time, creating a forked chain.

longest_chain_rule.name: Longest Chain Rule
longest_chain_rule.definition: Nodes always attempt to add blocks to the end of the longest chain to resolve accidental forks.

orphaned_block.name: Orphaned Block
orphaned_block.definition: A block on a shorter fork that gets inserted on the real chain later if its contents are not already there.

soft_fork.name: Soft Fork
soft_fork.definition: A fork where prior blocks are not invalidated and the old version of the blockchain software recognizes blocks from the new version as valid.

hard_fork.name: Hard Fork
hard_fork.definition: A fork where prior blocks may be invalidated and the old version of the blockchain software deems blocks from the new version as invalid.

testing_for_dependency_preservation.name: Testing for Dependency Preservation
testing_for_dependency_preservation.definition: A method to test if a decomposition is dependency preserving by checking if each member of F can be tested on one of the relations of the decomposition.

second_alternative_test_for_dependency_p.name: Second Alternative Test for Dependency Preservation
second_alternative_test_for_dependency_p.definition: A test that applies a specific procedure to each α → β in F to determine if the functional dependency β → α is preserved.

iteration_stops_when_max_change_in_p_val.name: Iteration Stops When Maximum Change in P[i] Value Below Cutoff
iteration_stops_when_max_change_in_p_val.definition: Iteration stops when the maximum change in any P[i] value in an iteration goes below some cutoff value.

tf_idf_scores.name: TF-IDF Scores
tf_idf_scores.definition: Scores used in combination with PageRank to judge the relevance of a document to a keyword query.

popularity_measure.name: Popularity Measure
popularity_measure.definition: Information about how often a site is visited is another useful measure of popularity.

user_clicks.name: User Clicks
user_clicks.definition: Search engines track what fraction of times users click on a page when it is returned as an answer.

anchor_text_term_frequency.name: Anchor Text Term Frequency
anchor_text_term_frequency.definition: Keywords that occur in the anchor text associated with the hyperlink to a page are viewed as very important and are given a higher term frequency.

disk_based_index.name: Disk-Based Index Structure
disk_based_index.definition: A structure used for indexing data stored on hard disk.

atomic_instructions.name: Atomic Instructions
atomic_instructions.definition: Instructions that can be executed without being interrupted, ensuring data consistency.

catalan_number.name: Catalan Number
catalan_number.definition: The number of binary trees with n nodes.

optimal_join_order.name: Optimal Join Order
optimal_join_order.definition: The best sequence of joins to minimize the cost of a query execution.

left_deep_join_tree.name: Left-Deep Join Tree
left_deep_join_tree.definition: A join tree where each join node has only one child.

bank_database.name: Bank Database
bank_database.definition: A relational database representing a banking system.

account_relation.name: Account Relation
account_relation.definition: A table in the relational database containing account information.

demanddriven_iterator.name: Demand-driven Iterator Model
demanddriven_iterator.definition: A model used in pipelined execution of operators in centralized database engines.

push.name: Push Model
push.definition: A model preferred for parallel execution of operators in a pipeline.

local_operation.name: Local Operation
local_operation.definition: An operation that can use the demand-driven iterator model to compute input for an exchange operator.

odbc_connection.name: ODBC Connection
odbc_connection.definition: A method for accessing data in a database that supports SQL.

hbase_api.name: HBase API Method
hbase_api.definition: A method for accessing data in a parallel data storage system that does not support SQL.

wrapper.name: Wrapper
wrapper.definition: A component that provides a view of data stored at a data source in a desired schema.

global_schema.name: Global Schema
global_schema.definition: A schema that is used across multiple data sources.

local_database_schema.name: Local Database Schema
local_database_schema.definition: A schema that is specific to a particular database.

web_service.name: Web Service
web_service.definition: A nonrelational data source that can be accessed using a wrapper.

flat_file.name: Flat File
flat_file.definition: A type of data source that can be accessed using a wrapper, e.g., web logs.

null_bitmap.name: Null Bitmap
null_bitmap.definition: A component used to indicate which attributes of the record have a null value.

request_get_parameter.name: request.getParameter()
request_get_parameter.definition: A method used to get the value of an attribute.

view_equivalence.name: View Equivalence
view_equivalence.definition: A concept where two schedules are considered equivalent if they produce the same result.

view_serializability.name: View Serializability
view_serializability.definition: A schedule is view serializable if it is view equivalent to a serial schedule.

conflict_serializability.name: Conflict Serializability
conflict_serializability.definition: A property of schedules where no two conflicting transactions can be swapped without changing the outcome.

blind_write.name: Blind Write
blind_write.definition: A write operation that occurs without a preceding read operation on the same data item.

timestamp_ordering.name: Timestamp Ordering
timestamp_ordering.definition: A method used to determine the serializability order of transactions based on their timestamps.

audit_trail.name: Audit Trail
audit_trail.definition: A component that records updates to tuples of a relation, such as what action was carried out, by whom, when, and from which IP address the request originated.

blockchain_techniques.name: Blockchain Techniques
blockchain_techniques.definition: Techniques that store logs in multiple machines and use a hashing mechanism to make it difficult for an intruder to modify or delete data without being detected.

multiversion_concurrency_control_schemes.name: Multiversion Concurrency Control Schemes
multiversion_concurrency_control_schemes.definition: Concurrency-control schemes that keep old copies of each data item to avoid delays and rejections.

concurrencycontrol_manager.name: Concurrency Control Manager
concurrencycontrol_manager.definition: A component responsible for selecting the version of a data item to be read.

magnetic_disks.name: Magnetic Disks
magnetic_disks.definition: A type of storage used in modern SAN and NAS systems.

ssds.name: SSDs
ssds.definition: Solid State Drives used in modern SAN and NAS systems.

san_nas_systems.name: SAN/NAS Systems
san_nas_systems.definition: Modern systems that support the use of a combination of magnetic disks and SSDs.

joinattrs.name: Join Attributes
joinattrs.definition: Attributes in R ∩ S used for joining two relations.

tr_tss.name: t_r ⋈ t_s
tr_tss.definition: The concatenation of the attributes of tuples t_r and t_s, followed by projecting out repeated attributes.

tuple_pointer.name: Tuple Pointer
tuple_pointer.definition: A pointer associated with each relation pointing to the current tuple being processed.

ss_set.name: S_s Set
ss_set.definition: A set of tuples with the same value for the join attributes.

concurrency.name: Concurrency
concurrency.definition: The ability of multiple transactions to run simultaneously.

resource_utilization.name: Resource Utilization
resource_utilization.definition: The extent to which processors and disks are used efficiently.

distributed_file_systems.name: Distributed File Systems
distributed_file_systems.definition: These allow files to be stored across a number of machines, while allowing access to files using a traditional file-system interface.

traditional_centralized_database.name: Traditional Centralized Database
traditional_centralized_database.definition: A traditional centralized database, which may not have any information about the other databases.

bulk_loading_of_b_plus_tree_indices.name: Bulk Loading of B+ Tree Indices
bulk_loading_of_b_plus_tree_indices.definition: Insertion of a large number of entries at a time into an index.

temporary_file.name: Temporary File
temporary_file.definition: A file used to store index entries temporarily.

sorted_file.name: Sorted File
sorted_file.definition: A file containing index entries sorted on the search key.

index_sequential_file_organization.name: Index-Sequential File Organization
index_sequential_file_organization.definition: A file organization method where the file is stored sequentially but an index is maintained to allow efficient access.

transaction_precedence_graph.name: Transaction Precedence Graph
transaction_precedence_graph.definition: A graph used to represent the order in which transactions execute.

read_write_conflict_edge.name: Read-Write Conflict Edge
read_write_conflict_edge.definition: An edge in the conflict graph representing a situation where a transaction T1 writes a version of an object and a transaction T2 subsequently reads an earlier version of the object.

system_catalog.name: System Catalog
system_catalog.definition: A component in the database system where histograms and other metadata are stored.

uniform_distribution_assumption.name: Uniform Distribution Assumption
uniform_distribution_assumption.definition: An assumption made by an optimizer when no histogram information is available, assuming each range has the same number of distinct values.

frequent_values_list.name: Frequent Values List
frequent_values_list.definition: A list of n most frequently occurring values for some n, along with their frequency counts, stored in the database to improve query estimates.

log_buffer.name: Log Buffer
log_buffer.definition: A buffer in main memory used to temporarily store log records before they are written to stable storage.

vision_task.name: Vision Task

classification_problem.name: Classification Problem
classification_problem.definition: Problems that involve identifying object occurrences in an image and assigning a class label to each identified object.

deep_neural_networks.name: Deep Neural Networks
deep_neural_networks.definition: Neural networks with a large number of layers that have proven very successful at such tasks.

deep_learning.name: Deep Learning
deep_learning.definition: Machine-learning techniques that create deep neural networks and train them on very large numbers of training instances.

current_node.name: Current Node
current_node.definition: The node being examined during the traversal of a B+ tree.

p_i_plus_one.name: P[i+1]

p_i.name: P[i]

io_operations.name: I/O Operations

worst_case_insertion.name: Worst Case Insertion
worst_case_insertion.definition: The process of inserting a new record into a B+ Tree under the most unfavorable conditions.

worst_case_deletion.name: Worst Case Deletion

log_n_2_n.name: Log ⌈n/2⌉ (N)
log_n_2_n.definition: The mathematical expression representing the number of I/O operations required for worst-case insertion and deletion operations in a B+ Tree.

check_and_mutate.name: checkAndMutate

log_based_protocol.name: Log-Based Protocol
log_based_protocol.definition: A type of consensus protocol whose goal is to maintain a log, to which records can be appended in a fault-tolerant manner.

raft_consensus_protocol.name: Raft Consensus Protocol
raft_consensus_protocol.definition: An example of a log-based protocol designed to be relatively easy to understand.

left_side.name: Left Side
left_side.definition: The set of attributes on the left-hand side of a functional dependency.

right_side.name: Right Side
right_side.definition: The set of attributes on the right-hand side of a functional dependency.

parallel_sort.name: Parallel Sort
parallel_sort.definition: A method for sorting a relation across multiple nodes.

rangepartitioning.name: Range Partitioning
rangepartitioning.definition: Partitioning a relation based on specific attributes.

centralized_database.name: Centralized Database System
centralized_database.definition: A system where the database administrator of the central site controls the database.

global_database_administrator.name: Global Database Administrator
global_database_administrator.definition: Responsible for the entire distributed database system.

local_database_administrator.name: Local Database Administrator
local_database_administrator.definition: Responsible for the database at each site in a distributed system.

homogeneous_distributed_database.name: Homogeneous Distributed Database System
homogeneous_distributed_database.definition: A system where nodes share a common global schema and run the same distributed database software.

traditional_database_query_processor.name: Traditional Database Query Processor
traditional_database_query_processor.definition: A component that acts as an interpreter to execute a query plan.

modern_mainmemory_database.name: Modern Mainmemory Database
modern_mainmemory_database.definition: A database that compiles query plans into machine code or intermediate level byte-code.

attribute_offset.name: Attribute Offset
attribute_offset.definition: The position of an attribute within a record.

function_call.name: Function Call
function_call.definition: A process where a function is called for each record processed by an operation.

recovery_and_concurrency_control.name: Recovery and Concurrency Control
recovery_and_concurrency_control.definition: A process involving repeated message sending and acknowledgment to ensure message delivery and handle failures.

complex_event_processing.name: Complex Event Processing System
complex_event_processing.definition: A system that executes actions when a subsequence of tuples matches a particular pattern.

oracle_event_processing.name: Oracle Event Processing
oracle_event_processing.definition: A popular complex event processing system.

microsoft_streaminsight.name: Microsoft StreamInsight
microsoft_streaminsight.definition: A popular complex event processing system.

flinkcep.name: FlinkCEP
flinkcep.definition: A component of the Apache Flink project that supports complex event processing.

lambda_architecture.name: Lambda Architecture
lambda_architecture.definition: An architecture that uses a copy of the input data for stream-processing and another copy for database storage.

grant_option.name: Grant Option
grant_option.definition: An additional privilege that allows a user to pass on their authorization to other users.

user.name: User
user.definition: A person or entity that is granted some form of authorization to access or modify resources.

authorization_graph.name: Authorization Graph
authorization_graph.definition: A graph representing the passing of a specific authorization from one user to another, where nodes are users and edges represent the granting of authorization.

forty_gigabit_ethernet.name: Forty-Gigabit Ethernet
forty_gigabit_ethernet.definition: A technology available at a higher cost than standard Ethernet and seeing increasing usage.

one_hundred_gigabit_ethernet.name: 100-Gigabit Ethernet
one_hundred_gigabit_ethernet.definition: A technology available at a higher cost than standard Ethernet and seeing increasing usage.

fiber_channel_protocol.name: Fiber Channel Protocol
fiber_channel_protocol.definition: A protocol standard designed for high-speed interconnection between storage systems and computers.

storage_area_networks.name: Storage Area Networks
storage_area_networks.definition: Networks implemented using the Fiber Channel Protocol standard.

infiniband_standard.name: Infiniband Standard
infiniband_standard.definition: A standard designed for interconnections with a data center, particularly for high-performance computing applications.

with_clause.name: WITH Clause
with_clause.definition: A component that provides a way of defining a temporary relation whose definition is available only to the query in which the with clause occurs.

maxbudget.name: maxbudget
maxbudget.definition: A temporary relation containing the results of the subquery defining the relation.

max_budget.name: max-budget
max_budget.definition: A temporary relation containing the results of the subquery defining the relation.

dept_total.name: dept_total
dept_total.definition: A temporary relation containing the sum of salaries grouped by department name.

dept_total_avg.name: dept_total_avg
dept_total_avg.definition: A temporary relation containing the average of the total salary at all departments.

local_partitioning_step.name: Local Partitioning Step
local_partitioning_step.definition: A step that partitions the output of the exchange operator locally.

hash_aggregation_operator.name: Hash Aggregation Operator
hash_aggregation_operator.definition: An operator that aggregates tuples pipelined from the exchange operator.

linesegment_data_type.name: Line Segment Data Type
linesegment_data_type.definition: A specialized data type used in a map database to represent line segments.

image_data_type.name: Image Data Type
image_data_type.definition: A specialized data type used to represent images.

stored_procedure.name: Stored Procedure
stored_procedure.definition: A procedure that is stored in the database and can be invoked from SQL statements.

business_logic.name: Business Logic
business_logic.definition: The rules and regulations that govern the operations of a business, such as university policies.

compound_statement.name: Compound Statement
compound_statement.definition: A statement of the form begin... end that may contain multiple SQL statements.

atomic_compound_statement.name: Atomic Compound Statement
atomic_compound_statement.definition: A compound statement of the form begin atomic... end that ensures all statements are executed as a single transaction.

while_statement.name: While Statement
while_statement.definition: A statement with the syntax: while boolean_expression do sequence_of_statements ; end while.

repeat_statement.name: Repeat Statement
repeat_statement.definition: A statement with the syntax: repeat sequence_of_statements ; until boolean_expression end repeat.

for_loop.name: For Loop
for_loop.definition: A loop that iterates over all the results of a query.

leave_statement.name: Leave Statement
leave_statement.definition: A statement used to exit the loop.

iterate_statement.name: Iterate Statement
iterate_statement.definition: A statement that starts the loop on the next tuple, from the beginning of the loop, skipping the remaining statements.

ifthen_else_statement.name: If-Then-Else Statement
ifthen_else_statement.definition: A conditional statement with the syntax: if boolean_expression then statement_or_compound_statement elseif boolean_expression then statement_or_compound_statement else statement_or_compound_statement.

randomized_retry.name: Randomized Retry Algorithm
randomized_retry.definition: A method used by Raft to elect leaders.

leader.name: Leader
leader.definition: A node that is elected to coordinate operations in the Raft consensus protocol.

term.name: Term
term.definition: A unique identifier for each election cycle in the Raft consensus protocol.

log_append_request.name: Log Append Request
log_append_request.definition: A message sent by a node to the current leader to append a record to the replicated log.

crabbing_protocol.name: Crabbing Protocol
crabbing_protocol.definition: A protocol for concurrency control in index structures.

child_node.name: Child Node
child_node.definition: A node in an index structure that is a direct descendant of another node.

parent_node.name: Parent Node
parent_node.definition: A node in an index structure that has one or more child nodes.

relational_representation_of_crosstabs.name: Relational Representation of CrossTabs
relational_representation_of_crosstabs.definition: A method to represent cross-tabulations using relational databases.

sales_relation.name: Sales Relation
sales_relation.definition: A relation that stores sales data.

city_hierarchy.name: City Hierarchy
city_hierarchy.definition: A hierarchical representation of cities, states, countries, and regions.

multiple_relations.name: Multiple Relations
multiple_relations.definition: Multiple relations mapping values in one level of the hierarchy to values at the next level.

single_relation_city_hierarchy.name: Single Relation City Hierarchy
single_relation_city_hierarchy.definition: A single relation storing city, state, country, and region information with unique identifiers.

log_record_operation_begin.name: Log Record (Operation Begin)
log_record_operation_begin.definition: A log record created before an operation to modify an index, containing the transaction ID and operation identifier.

operation_end_log_record.name: Operation End Log Record
operation_end_log_record.definition: A log record created when an operation ends, containing the transaction ID, operation identifier, and undo information.

logical_logging.name: Logical Logging
logical_logging.definition: Logging method used for undo operations, recording information about operations such as insertions and deletions.

physical_logging.name: Physical Logging
physical_logging.definition: Logging method used for redo operations, recording old-value and new-value information for each update.

user_defined_types.name: User-Defined Types
user_defined_types.definition: Structured types created using SQL extensions that can include references and tables.

person_type.name: Person Type
person_type.definition: A user-defined type with fields ID, name, and address.

people_table.name: People Table
people_table.definition: A table containing tuples of the Person type.

array_types.name: Array Types
array_types.definition: Types that represent arrays of elements, with varying syntaxes across different database systems.

integer_array.name: Integer Array
integer_array.definition: An array of integers without a specified size, denoted as integer[] in PostgreSQL.

varray_type.name: Varray Type
varray_type.definition: An array of a fixed number of elements, denoted as varray(10) of integer in Oracle.

tablevalued_types.name: Table-Valued Types
tablevalued_types.definition: Types that represent tables of data, allowing for more complex data structures within a single column.

interest_table.name: Interest Table
interest_table.definition: A table-valued type with fields topic and degree_of_interest.

users_table.name: Users Table
users_table.definition: A table containing columns ID, name, and interests, where interests is a table-valued type.

methods.name: Methods
methods.definition: Functions or procedures associated with user-defined types, which are supported by only a few database systems.

r_tree_insertion.name: R-Tree Insertion Algorithm
r_tree_insertion.definition: An algorithm used for inserting new elements into an R-Tree while ensuring the tree remains balanced and bounding boxes are consistent.

b_plus_tree_insertion.name: B+ Tree Insertion Algorithm
b_plus_tree_insertion.definition: An algorithm used for inserting new elements into a B+ Tree while ensuring the tree remains balanced.

sec_time_slot.name: sec_time_slot
sec_time_slot.definition: A schema used in representing relationship sets in an E-R diagram.

sec_class.name: sec_class
sec_class.definition: A schema used in representing relationship sets in an E-R diagram.

mfence_instruction.name: mfence Instruction
mfence_instruction.definition: An instruction that ensures both ordering and visibility of memory operations.

sfence_instruction.name: sfence Instruction
sfence_instruction.definition: An instruction that ensures that all writes before it are visible before any reads after it.

lfence_instruction.name: lfence Instruction
lfence_instruction.definition: An instruction that ensures that all reads after it are only from memory and not from the cache.

coherent_cache.name: Coherent Cache
coherent_cache.definition: A property where writes are propagated in order and reads see the most recent values.

prediction.name: Prediction Model
prediction.definition: A model built using past data to predict future outcomes.

decision_tree.name: Decision Tree
decision_tree.definition: A specific type of prediction model studied in this chapter.

loan_default_history.name: Loan Default History
loan_default_history.definition: Past data on loan defaults used to train prediction models.

customer_features.name: Customer Features
customer_features.definition: Key characteristics of customers used in prediction models, such as salary, education level, job history.

bank.name: Bank
bank.definition: An organization that provides loans and analyzes customer data.

online_advertiser.name: Online Advertiser
online_advertiser.definition: An entity that shows advertisements to users based on their behavior.

sales_history.name: Sales History
sales_history.definition: Past data on sales used to predict future sales.

operation_consistency.name: Operation Consistency
operation_consistency.definition: Any operation should not see a database state that reflects only some of the updates of another operation.

tuple_t1.name: Tuple T1
tuple_t1.definition: A specific tuple in relation R with primary key A.

semijoin_strategy.definition: A strategy where if the corresponding bit is set to 1 in b, the r2 tuple is accepted (added to the result relation), and otherwise it is rejected.

result_relation.name: Result Relation
result_relation.definition: The relation computed above, which is a superset of or equal to r2 ⋈ r1, sent to site s1.

r1.name: r1
r1.definition: A data source involved in the join operation.

r2.name: r2
r2.definition: A data source involved in the join operation.

site_s1.name: Site s1
site_s1.definition: The site where the join r1 ⋈ result is computed to get the required join result.

massively_parallel_relational_database.name: Massively Parallel Relational Database
massively_parallel_relational_database.definition: A database designed to handle massive scale and support easy addition of more nodes without significant disruption.

logical_undo_log_records.name: Logical Undo Log Records
logical_undo_log_records.definition: Records used for performing logical undo operations.

idempotent_operations.name: Idempotent Operations
idempotent_operations.definition: Operations that give the same result when executed multiple times.

unspent_transaction.name: Unspent Transaction
unspent_transaction.definition: A transaction that has not been used as an input in any other transaction.

double_spend_transaction.name: Double-Spend Transaction
double_spend_transaction.definition: A transaction attempting to spend the output of a previously unspent transaction.

ethereum.name: Ethereum
ethereum.definition: A decentralized platform that runs smart contracts.

account.name: Account
account.definition: A record in the blockchain that holds the current balance.

single_user_database_systems.name: Single-User Database Systems
single_user_database_systems.definition: Database systems used by a single person, typically with one processor and one or two disks.

multiuser_systems.name: Multiuser Systems
multiuser_systems.definition: Systems serving a large number of users who are connected to the system remotely.

server_systems.name: Server Systems
server_systems.definition: Multiuser systems that serve a large number of users remotely.

ledger_entry.name: Ledger Entry
ledger_entry.definition: An entry added to a ledger maintained by the bank.

bank_ledger.name: Bank Ledger
bank_ledger.definition: A ledger maintained by the bank to record transactions.

blockchain_based_distributed_ledger.name: Blockchain-Based Distributed Ledger
blockchain_based_distributed_ledger.definition: A ledger cooperatively maintained among several parties using digital signatures for proof of authenticity.

large_corporation_supplier_network.name: Large Corporation Supplier Network
large_corporation_supplier_network.definition: A network of a large corporation and its suppliers who maintain data about product and component locations.

atomic_commit.name: Atomic Commit
atomic_commit.definition: The ability to commit multiple updates to a single row atomically.

secondary_indices.name: Secondary Indices
secondary_indices.definition: Indices used to quickly locate data items.

megastore.name: Megastore
megastore.definition: A parallel key-value store system developed by Google.

isolation_property.name: Isolation Property
isolation_property.definition: Database systems must provide mechanisms to isolate transactions from the effects of other concurrently executing transactions.

serializability_concept.definition: Chapter 18 describes several concurrency-control techniques that help implement the isolation property by means of a concept called serializability.

durability_property.name: Durability Property
durability_property.definition: Once a transaction has been committed, its effects are permanent.

concurrency_control_techniques.name: Concurrency Control Techniques
concurrency_control_techniques.definition: Several techniques described in Chapter 18 help implement the isolation property.

recovery_management_component.definition: A component of the database system that implements the atomicity and durability properties.

nearest_neighbor_queries.name: Nearest Neighbor Queries
nearest_neighbor_queries.definition: Queries that find the closest element to a given point.

line_segments.name: Line Segments
line_segments.definition: Geometric objects that connect two points in space.

rectangles.name: Rectangles
rectangles.definition: Two-dimensional shapes with four straight sides and four right angles.

polygons.name: Polygons
polygons.definition: Closed plane figures bounded by straight lines.

slotted_page_record_organization.name: Slotted Page Record Organization
slotted_page_record_organization.definition: A method of organizing records within a page where each record is identified by a unique slot number.

cost_of_evaluating_expression.definition: The total cost of evaluating an expression, including the costs of all operations and writing intermediate results to disk.

blocking_factor.definition: The number of records of the result relation that will fit in a block.

number_of_blocks_written_out_br.definition: Estimated as n_r / f_r, where n_r is the estimated number of tuples in the result relation r and f_r is the blocking factor of the result relation.

tracking_data_received_early.name: Tracking Data Received Early
tracking_data_received_early.definition: Tracking the data received earlier is important to ensure duplicate tuples are detected and eliminated by the receiving node.

parallel_execution.name: Parallel Execution

scaleup.name: Scaleup

web_scale_application.name: Web-Scale Application
web_scale_application.definition: An application that runs on data management systems combining support for parallelism and distribution.

tableau.name: Tableau

fusioncharts.name: FusionCharts
fusioncharts.definition: A tool for web-based data visualization and dashboard creation.

plotly.name: Plotly
plotly.definition: A tool for web-based data visualization and dashboard creation.

datawrapper.name: Datawrapper
datawrapper.definition: A tool for web-based data visualization and dashboard creation.

google_charts.name: Google Charts
google_charts.definition: A tool for web-based data visualization and dashboard creation.

ldap_data_interchange_format.name: LDAP Data Interchange Format
ldap_data_interchange_format.definition: A file format defined by LDAP for storing and exchanging information.

alias.name: Alias

bottom_up_b_plus_tree_construction.definition: A method of constructing a B+ tree where the leaves are built first and then merged upwards.

tuple_at_a_time_insertion.name: Tuple-at-a-Time Insertion
tuple_at_a_time_insertion.definition: A method of inserting data into a database one tuple at a time.

space_efficient_data.name: Space-Efficient Data Structure
space_efficient_data.definition: A type of data structure designed to use minimal space while still being effective.

array_representation.name: Array Representation
array_representation.definition: A representation of the free-space map using an array where each entry corresponds to a block in the file.

postgresql_free_space_map_entry.name: PostgreSQL Free-Space Map Entry
postgresql_free_space_map_entry.definition: An entry in the free-space map in PostgreSQL that stores a value representing the free-space fraction of a block.

distributed_consensus_protocol.name: Distributed Consensus Protocol
distributed_consensus_protocol.definition: A protocol used to keep logs synchronized without the need for version numbering.

chain_replication_protocol.name: Chain Replication Protocol
chain_replication_protocol.definition: A variant of the primary copy scheme where replicas are ordered and updates are forwarded sequentially.

in_memory_buffer.name: In-Memory Buffer
in_memory_buffer.definition: A component in database systems that stores frequently accessed data in memory to improve performance.

random_io_cost.name: Random I/O Cost
random_io_cost.definition: The cost associated with reading data from a specific location on a disk.

wall_clock_time.name: Wall-Clock Time
wall_clock_time.definition: The actual elapsed time measured by a clock, as opposed to CPU time.

multiple_disks.name: Multiple Disks
multiple_disks.definition: A system configuration where data is stored across multiple physical disks.

disk_page_reads.name: Disk Page Reads
disk_page_reads.definition: The process of reading data from a specific page on a disk.

acknowledge_t_message.definition: A message sent by a node to the coordinator at the end of the second phase of the Two-Phase Commit Protocol.

tuning.name: Tuning
tuning.definition: Typically done in the context of applications, and can be done at the database system layer, or outside the database system.

profiling_application_code.name: Profiling Application Code
profiling_application_code.definition: Finding code blocks with heavy CPU consumption and rewriting them to reduce CPU load.

load_balancer.name: Load Balancer
load_balancer.definition: A component used to route requests to one of the application servers, ensuring session continuity.

web_application_interfaces.name: Web Application Interfaces
web_application_interfaces.definition: Interfaces that can be tuned to improve responsiveness.

database_system_tuning_levels.name: Database System Tuning Levels
database_system_tuning_levels.definition: Levels of database tuning that are under the control of application developers.

data_warehouse_schema.name: Data Warehouse Schema
data_warehouse_schema.definition: A schema designed for data analysis in a data warehouse.

dimension_table.name: Dimension Table

dimension_attribute.name: Dimension Attribute
dimension_attribute.definition: An attribute that is used to group and view measure attributes.

measure_attribute.name: Measure Attribute

multidimensional_data.name: Multidimensional Data
multidimensional_data.definition: Data that can be modeled using dimension attributes and measure attributes.

negative_sentiment_tweet.name: Negative Sentiment Tweet

advertisement_campaign.name: Advertisement Campaign
advertisement_campaign.definition: An advertisement campaign launched by a company.

column_store.name: Column Store
column_store.definition: A type of database storage that organizes data by columns rather than rows.

denormalized_relation.name: Denormalized Relation
denormalized_relation.definition: A relation that repeats certain attributes to improve query performance.

irreversibility.name: Irreversibility

transaction_validation.name: Transaction Validation

index_on_unspent_transactions.name: Index on Unspent Transactions
